stories.title: 800-year-old 'Mazar' razed overnight:Bulldozers clear land in Etawah; saplings planted across site
stories.summary: Syed Baba's shrine in Etawah, UP, was demolished by a bulldozer on Wednesday night. When villagers arrived on Thursday morning, there was no trace of the shrine left. The entire land had been leveled. Waist-high plants had been planted. The place looked like a jungle. Seeing this, people couldn't believe that a shrine had stood there just 12 hours earlier. On Wednesday evening at 6 PM, a Forest Department team arrived with three bulldozers. More than 20 policemen were deployed on the path leading to the shrine. Movement of anyone was restricted. After this, the shrine was demolished in 7 hours. The bulldozer action continued until 1 AM. The shrine's caretaker claims that the shrine was 800 years old. The Forest Department states that the shrine was built on government land, which is why action was taken. This shrine, built over 3000 square feet, was located in the Fisher forest area of the ravines, one and a half kilometers from Etawah city. The shrine was famous by the name of Beehad Wale Syed Baba. In January, a complaint about the shrine was made on the CM portal. Following this, the forest department investigated and issued instructions to remove the shrine. The caretaker of the shrine went to the forest department's court, but their appeal was rejected. See 3 pictures- Know the full story in 5 points There is no record of who built the shrine or when it was built. Every year in February, an Urs (festival) was organized at the shrine, in which 5 to 7 thousand people participated. This time, the Urs did not take place in February. There is no official record available of when the shrine was built, who built it, or when it was established. Forest department officials also do not have any record related to its construction. The Forest Department says that over time, construction gradually increased on the protected forest land and later a permanent structure was erected here. This entire process took place without any statutory permission, hence it has been considered illegal construction. Maulana says - Claim of it being the tomb of Muhammad Ghori's general is false The tomb is looked after by Fazle Ilahi, a resident of Akalganj, Etawah city. His associate Maulana Nadeem said that this tomb is about 800 years old. Some people claim it to be the tomb of Muhammad Ghori's general Shamsuddin, but this claim is completely false and baseless. He said - Historical documents state that in 1194, a war took place in Etawah between the Islamic invader Muhammad Ghori and Sumer Singh, the commander of King Jaichand of Kannauj. In this, Ghori's general Shamsuddin and many Muslim soldiers were killed. Some of them were buried in Bais Khwaja, but no one has any information on how Shamsuddin's tomb was built in Fisher Forest.

stories.title: Boyfriend forces nursing student to take abortion pills, she dies:Buys medicines after watching YouTube; flees Varanasi hostel
stories.summary: A 19-year-old nursing student died in Varanasi after consuming abortion pills. She was 3 months pregnant. Her boyfriend had pressured her into taking the medicine. On Wednesday morning at 11:30 AM, the student's blood-soaked body was found on the hostel stairs. An electrician who came to work there first saw the student lying unconscious. When he shouted, the guard and people nearby arrived. The student was taken to Shiv Surgical Nursing Home, where doctors declared her dead. Police examined the student's call details. They spoke to her family members and the hostel guard. The guard stated that the student used to meet Mohammad Sameer, a resident of Kariyav Mirganj, Jaunpur, at the hostel. Police traced his location and arrested Sameer from his home late Wednesday evening. Upon strict interrogation, he confessed. During police interrogation, the accused stated that he had bought abortion pills after watching YouTube. After taking the medicine, his girlfriend experienced severe stomach pain. Vomiting and bleeding started. She asked to be taken to the hospital. Then she started running down the stairs herself, fainted and fell. Her clothes were soaked in blood. I panicked and left her, fleeing to my home in Jaunpur. The student's father is a constable. He is posted in Chandauli. He lives in Kashi with his family. He has two sons. The student was a GNM second-year student. Her boyfriend, Mohammad Sameer, also studies in the same college. He is a nursing third-year student. Boyfriend said - talked to doctors, but no one was ready for an abortion The boyfriend told during the interrogation that they had been in a relationship for two years. They used to travel together during holidays. One day, she told him that she was pregnant. An ultrasound confirmed it. She was three months pregnant. They talked to doctors, but no one was ready for an abortion without the consent of family members. After this, both of them planned the abortion themselves. Bought Abortion Pills After Watching YouTube The boyfriend said - Being medical students, they first read books, but couldn't decide anything. After this, they watched YouTube. After watching several channels, they agreed to take abortion pills. They also saw the method of taking the medicine on YouTube, then bought a branded medicine. It was decided that the student would take the medicine on Wednesday. On Wednesday morning at 9 AM, she reached the hostel with food for both of us from home. After coming into the room, she was scared and nervous. When asked to take the medicine, she refused. When pressured, she said - let's get married, but I didn't listen to her. Against her will, I forcibly made her take the medicine. The dose of medicine was high. Bleeding started an hour later. Half an hour later, her condition worsened even more. She said, "Take me to the hospital." Before I could say anything, she ran out of the room. I was scared seeing the blood The boyfriend said - blood was continuously flowing from her private part. The lift was closed due to a power outage. Because of this, she started going down the stairs. Then she felt dizzy due to bleeding and fell. I was scared seeing the blood. I came up to my room, locked it, and fled to my home in Jaunpur by bus. Student's abortion was also done 7 months ago According to the police, painkillers and other medicines were found in the student's bag. Her boyfriend said that the student had an abortion 7 months ago as well. Videos and photos were found on the boyfriend's phone. Chatting done with the student has also been recovered. Guard said - The student was coming to the hostel continuously for two days The guard of the boys' hostel said that the girl had been coming to the hostel continuously for the last two days. She had also come on Tuesday. She made three-four rounds from the grocery store on the road opposite to the tree inside the campus and wandered alone for a long time. On Wednesday morning at 9:20 AM, she went straight to the room, climbing the stairs alone. Later, she was found covered in blood. ACP Sarnath Vidyut Saxena said- The student's body was post-mortemed by a panel of two doctors, and its videography was also done. The boyfriend has been arrested and is being interrogated.

stories.title: Baraat on Bulldozer:Groom smokes cigarette as band and dancers follow; Moradabad Police issue fine
stories.summary: In Moradabad, the groom set off for the wedding procession on a bulldozer. The bulldozer sometimes lifted the wedding guests 10 feet up and sometimes brought them down to the road. During this, the groom kept smoking cigarettes and blowing rings. He kept dancing. He kept gesturing to the children sitting with him to dance. A video of the groom going to his in-laws' house on a bulldozer was recorded by a friend of the groom and uploaded on Instagram. The video quickly went viral. In the video, 15 wedding guests are seen sitting on the bulldozer with the groom. The groom is smoking a cigarette and blowing smoke into the air. When the police investigated the video, it was found that the wedding procession had gone from Umri Kalan village in Kanth to Sahaspur village in Bijnor two days earlier, on June 8. Taking action, the police issued a challan for the bulldozer on Wednesday, June 10. The matter falls under the Kanth police station area. See 2 pictures First, understand the whole matter step-by-step- Usman, a resident of Umri Kalan in Kanth police station area, was engaged to a girl from Sahaspur village in Bijnor. The wedding was on June 8. On Monday afternoon, after completing the 'ghudchadhi' (groom's procession on horseback) ritual with the baraatis (wedding guests) from his home, the groom rode on a bulldozer. During this, about 15 baraatis also climbed onto the bulldozer with him. Bhangra music played in front, and the bulldozer followed behind. The groom was seen dancing while sitting on the bulldozer. The youths sitting with him were seen dancing to film songs. Now read, what is visible in the video It can be seen in the video that the bulldozer is decorated with flowers. The groom, wearing a white sherwani, is sitting on its front part. Garlands of notes are around his neck. Along with the groom, about 10 to 15 people are also riding on the bulldozer. Some of them are children. The groom is smoking a cigarette and blowing smoke rings. The youths sitting with him are dancing to film songs. Bhangra is playing in front, and the bulldozer is moving behind. Some people are also making videos. A song is playing in the background - 'I haven't come here to interfere in anyone's business...' Video 2 days old, bulldozer will be seized SP Rural Kunwar Akash Singh said- The video of going to the wedding by bulldozer is from June 8. Taking action in this matter, the bulldozer has been challaned. Action will be taken to find and seize the bulldozer.

stories.title: Monkey attacks man outside exam centre:Left arm vein cut; accompanying daughter for UP Police recruitment exam in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: A father who came to Gorakhpur to help his daughter take the UP Constable recruitment exam was bitten and severely injured by a monkey. In the attack, a vein in his left hand was severed, causing continuous bleeding. Upon receiving information, the police on duty immediately took the injured person to Nehru Hospital at BRD Medical College. There, doctors brought the situation under control after providing treatment. It is being told that Vishambhar, a resident of Maharajganj district, had arrived at a school center in Pipraich with his daughter Priya on Wednesday. After the exam started, he was sitting in a garden about 200 meters away from the center, waiting for his daughter to come out. Suddenly, a black monkey attacked him. After the incident, the forest department team started searching for the monkey, but its whereabouts are still unknown. Know the full story According to information, Priya, daughter of Vishambhar Prasad, a resident of Gopalpur village in Pharenda police station area of Maharajganj district, had her constable recruitment exam in the first shift on Wednesday. To help her take the exam, he took his daughter to the Maharana Pratap Krishi Inter College center in Pipraich. His daughter entered and started giving the paper inside. Meanwhile, Vishambhar was sitting in a garden about 200 meters away from the center, waiting for his daughter to come out. Around 12 noon, a black monkey suddenly arrived there. The monkey hovered around for some time The monkey hovered around for some time and then suddenly attacked Vishambhar. In the attack, a vein in his right hand was cut, causing him to bleed profusely. After the incident, there was chaos among the people present nearby. Upon receiving the information, Sub-Inspector Shailendra Yadav, who was on duty, reached the spot and immediately took the injured person to BRD Medical College. There, doctors treated him and stopped the bleeding from the vein in his hand. Upon learning about the incident, the injured person's family also reached the hospital. After her exam ended, his daughter Priya also arrived at the hospital. Meanwhile, upon police information, a team from the forest department also reached the spot and is engaged in searching for and monitoring the monkey in the area. However, it has not been found yet.

stories.title: UP govt promotes 36 PCS officers to IAS:Anju Kataria’s promotion also confirmed; official orders expected shortly
stories.summary: 36 PCS officers from UP will be promoted. They will also be assigned new responsibilities. The officers to be promoted include Resident Commissioner, Special Secretary, Additional Commissioner, ADM, Secretary, and officers from several development authorities. The promotion of Harish Chandra (1997 batch), Prabhunath (1999 batch), Anju Katiyar (2002 batch), and Amar Pal Singh (2004 batch) has been confirmed. Additionally, many officers from the 2010, 2011, and 2012 batches will also benefit from promotion. The names of officers to be promoted include Alok Verma, Dr. Vishram, Pushpraj Singh, Vivek Srivastava, Yoganand Pandey, Amit Kumar, Dr. Sunil Kumar Verma, Garima Swaroop, and Sandeep Kumar, among others. This decision will bring about administrative changes at the district, divisional, and departmental levels in many areas. The promoted officers will soon be assigned new responsibilities in their positions. She has also been a topper of the UPPSC examination. In 2018, she was the Examination Controller at the UP Public Service Commission (UPPSC). During this period, the case of the LT Grade teacher recruitment examination paper leak came to light. The UP STF arrested her in May 2019 on charges of alleged involvement in the case. After her arrest, the state government suspended her. She remained in jail for several months. After about 8 months, she was granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in 2020. Later, she was reinstated in service. PCS Rakesh Kumar Patel also promoted Rakesh Kumar Patel is a PCS officer of the 2010 batch. After promotion, he will be inducted into the Indian Administrative Service (IAS). In the recent promotion, he will be assigned new responsibilities. Rakesh Kumar Patel, a resident of Maharajganj, is currently serving as Additional Commissioner (Judicial)-IV in Lucknow division. Prior to this, he has also served as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) in Pratapgarh. From July 2024 to July 2025, he was posted as Additional District Magistrate (ADM) in Kasganj. Considering his long experience in the administrative field, he has been promoted.

stories.title: SP MP raises issue of posts on Akhilesh’s daughter:Former minister says opposition does not target family members; calls it cheap politics
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party members are angry over objectionable posts on social media targeting Akhilesh Yadav's 23-year-old elder daughter, Aditi Yadav. Samajwadi Party MP from Ghosi seat in Mau, Rajiv Rai, on Wednesday, criticised the BJP and UP Police. He said, "This is the lowest level of politics and the pinnacle of mental derangement. Obscene and vulgar posts are being made on social media about former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav's daughter. UP Police has not taken any action yet. Is it because she is not the daughter of a BJP leader? Shame on you." Former minister and Samajwadi Party leader from Ayodhya, Tej Narayan Pandey (Pawan Pandey), has blamed the BJP for this. Pawan Pandey released a video on X and said, When Akhilesh Yadav raised questions about theft in the offerings of the Ram Temple, instead of giving factual answers to the allegations, BJP leaders resorted to personal attacks. Targeting Akhilesh's family is cheap politics. This is not just an attack on a political family, but an assault on the dignity of every daughter, every sister, and every mother in the state. In this matter, SP workers have filed a complaint at Hazratganj Kotwali in Lucknow. They have demanded strict action by registering an FIR against those who posted against Aditi Yadav. Now read in detail Pawan Pandey said- An attack on the dignity of every daughter, sister, and mother in the state Pawan Pandey said, instead of answering questions related to the Ram Temple donation amount, some BJP leaders and supporters are targeting the families of political opponents. It is extremely unfortunate that those who (the BJP) claim to be the biggest protectors of Sanatan culture are the ones who, in political vendetta, do things that hurt the dignity of women and daughters. In Sanatan tradition, women are considered a form of power, respect, and worship, but in the BJP's politics, when it becomes difficult to answer, character assassination and mudslinging at families become the easiest weapon. Those who are writing this must also have been born to a mother; they must also have a sister, a wife; how would they feel if something like this happened to their family? Every baseless accusation made against Akhilesh Yadav's family is not just an attack on a political family, but an assault on the dignity of every daughter, every sister, and every mother in the state. This is proof of that double standard, where slogans of 'women's respect' are raised from stages, and behind the scenes, women's dignity is made a political weapon. You are very adept at slandering others' mothers, sisters, daughters, wives, and using inappropriate words. However, when the same thing happens to you, you don't hesitate to beat your chest and cry. SP MP from Sitapur, Anand Bhadauria, said, Slinging mud on character is the pride of cowards, respecting daughters is the identity of India. Those who want to defame a daughter with fabricated stories, do they also know the consequences of public anger? SP spokesperson said - Aditi understands her good and bad SP spokesperson Nahid Lari Khan has responded to those posting on social media. She wrote on X, Aditi Yadav is a promising and highly qualified child. She has a very good understanding of right and wrong. Since she is the daughter of Akhilesh Yadav, the biggest leader of UP, the third largest state in the country, and a great warrior of PDA, the absurd people of an absurd party are writing absurd things about Aditi. It is possible that those who write cheap things have had such unfortunate incidents happen in their homes. Perhaps that is why, out of resentment, they are writing cheap things about the family of a big leader. Don't write such things. Everyone has daughters and sisters in their homes. Learn to respect women. This is not an insult to Aditi, but an insult to every daughter and sister in the country. Lohini Vahini said - if no action is taken, a big protest will be launched Raj Sahni, National Vice President of Samajwadi Lohia Vahini, said that extremely objectionable posts have been made against Aditi Yadav, daughter of SP President Akhilesh Yadav, on social media platforms. He demanded that an FIR be registered against anti-social elements spreading misleading and character-assassinating propaganda. He has handed over all evidence related to the matter and social media screenshots to the police. He said that if the police do not take action against such people, a protest will be launched. Raj Sahni said that our emotions are directly connected to Akhilesh Yadav and his family. Making such serious and baseless allegations against a daughter is extremely shameful. If someone makes even a small comment on a leader of the ruling party, immediate action is taken against them. But the character assassination of the former Chief Minister's daughter is being done on social media, and no action is being taken on it. SP spokesperson said - Will file cases against each and every one SP National Spokesperson Fakhrul Hasan Chand said, As soon as people of the party with 'character, conduct, and face' get stuck in any issue, they descend to the lowest level of their politics. They start making indecent comments on the members of the Samajwadi family. Sometimes, a BJP mayor speaks about the late mother of our respected national president, who is a leader for all of us. Now, BJP leaders and workers are commenting on social media about the daughter of the respected national president with their low, cheap mentality. The way one post after another was written on social media, BJP's power is behind it. BJP is engaging in low-level politics. Listen carefully, those who write about the Samajwadi family on social media will not be spared. We will file a case against each and every one. If it's not registered at the police station, we will get it registered under 173(3) BNSS. Be prepared, you will definitely face us in court.

stories.title: Devotee claims Baba Neem Karoli’s 'slap' transformed his life:Burn injury healed instantly; entire wedding party saved in bus accident
stories.summary: Numerous extraordinary experiences associated with Kainchi Dham and Baba Neem Karoli (Neem Karoli Baba) continue to be narrated by devotees, who regard them as direct manifestations of divine grace. One such account comes from Delhi resident Ravindra Joshi, also known as “Rabbu Dada,” who dedicated his life to the service of the saint. According to memoirs cited in Vijay Chhabaria and Dr. Deepak Patwardhan’s book Divya Anubhuti, Rabbu Dada was not only a devoted follower but also actively involved in temple construction and idol installation work across locations ranging from Taos in the United States to Bawaniya in Gujarat. Rabbu Dada first met Baba Neem Karoli during the summer of 1958 while visiting Nainital. Hearing stories of the saint’s miracles at Hanumangarhi, he felt a strong desire to meet him. For three days, Baba reportedly ignored him completely, neither speaking to him nor calling him. This behaviour left the devotee confused and restless. On the fourth day, Baba finally called him during evening prayers and remarked that the boy had been wondering why he was being ignored. “Slap” described as moment of spiritual awakening According to Rabbu Dada, Baba suddenly struck him on the head—an act he describes not as punishment but as a form of blessing. He claims that in that moment he experienced tears, mental stillness, and a sense of unity with the guru, feeling no separation between himself and the saint. Healing burn injury with a blanket Rabbu Dada also recounts several other miraculous incidents. Once, while frying puris in the kitchen, hot boiling ghee spilled onto his hand, causing severe burns. Before he could express the pain, Baba immediately asked if his hand was burnt. Upon confirmation, Baba placed his hand inside his blanket and pressed it, saying, “It is fine now, go.” According to the devotee, the pain and burning sensation disappeared instantly. Divine experiences and Uncanny predictions The devotee further recalls that Baba often consumed offerings from devotees throughout the day, tasting food prepared by different families as a gesture of blessing. He also recounts how his aunt, initially a devotee of Lord Krishna but sceptical of saints, reportedly saw Baba as Lord Krishna Himself, after which her doubts disappeared. Rabbu Dada describes another experience where Baba appeared to know about his personal habits without being told, reinforcing his belief in the saint’s omniscience. Bus accident incident during marriage journey In 1970, when Rabbu Dada’s marriage was arranged, Baba advised him to travel by train. However, he chose to travel by a private bus, which later met with an accident and overturned. Fortunately, no one suffered serious injuries. Later, Baba is said to have remarked humorously that he had to “protect everyone on the bus” since his instructions were not followed. Dream that turned into reality Rabbu Dada also recounts a dream in which he saw Baba standing near a staircase at a house in Allahabad. The next morning, he found Baba at the exact same location, an event he considers one of the most unforgettable moments of his life. Establishment of Kainchi Dham and later legacy After Baba’s passing, devotees installed his idol at Kainchi Dham. On June 15, 1976, the consecration ceremony (Pran Pratishtha) of the idol was performed with Vedic rituals. Kainchi Dham, located near Bhowali in Uttarakhand’s Nainital district, was established by Baba Neem Karoli in the 1960s along the banks of the Shipra River. It is now widely known for its spiritual significance and serene natural surroundings. Subsequently, temples dedicated to Baba were also established in Vrindavan, Lucknow, Delhi, Shimla and other locations. “Once I hold someone’s hand, I never leave them” According to Rabbu Dada, Baba Neem Karoli often assured devotees that he never abandons those he takes under his guidance. He considers the “blessing” he received after the famous slap as the greatest support of his life. As devotees recall, Baba would often say: “If I once hold someone’s hand, I never leave them.”

stories.title: Rainfall recorded in 10 cities across UP:Lucknow remains cloudy; storm and rain warning for all districts over next 3 days
stories.summary: The pre-monsoon rain spell has started in UP. Early Wednesday morning, Prayagraj, Meerut, Saharanpur, Gonda, and Bijnor experienced heavy rain with strong winds. The capital, Lucknow and the surrounding areas remained cloudy. The sun also appeared intermittently. However, due to humidity in the air, there is some relief from the heat. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms, strong winds, and rain in all 75 districts of the state today. A warning for hailstones and lightning has been issued in some areas. According to the IMD, a new Western Disturbance will become active within 24 hours. This will intensify the pre-monsoon activity. The weather will remain similar for the next three days. Earlier, a storm with a speed of 90 (kmph) hit Bareilly late Wednesday night. There was heavy rainfall. Roads were waterlogged up to about 2 feet. Trees and hoardings fell in many places. As a precautionary measure, electricity was cut off in the entire city. Early morning, Noida-Ghaziabad and Sambhal had rain with strong winds. Lucknow scientist Atul Singh said- A new western disturbance is becoming active in UP. This will accelerate pre-monsoon activities. Thunderstorms and rain will continue till June 15-16. The monsoon will enter the state by its scheduled time, i.e., June 20. It will cover the entire UP within 10 days.

stories.title: UP govt schools to offer convent-style education soon:39 CM composite schools under construction; admissions from 2027 with smart classes
stories.summary: Do you want to educate your child in a good convent school, but hesitate seeing the skyrocketing fees? Then leave your worries behind. The UP government is going to make this dream of yours come true. 'CM Composite Schools' are now being opened in the state to provide world-class education like convents at very low fees. Here, there will be high-tech smart classes, science, robotics labs, and digital libraries. There will be professional teachers who can compete with private schools. Your child will get exactly the same environment as they would in convent schools. How CM Composite Schools will change the image of government schools, 39 CM Composite Schools are being built in the first phase Currently, in UP, there are separate schools for Primary, Upper Primary, and Secondary levels. However, in a Composite Model School, there will be classes from Pre-Primary (Nursery) to 12th grade. This means that primary, junior, high school, and intermediate education will be provided on the same campus. Currently, there is a plan to open 2 CM Composite Schools in every district of the state. After this, similar schools will be opened at the block level and then at the Nyay Panchayat level. The government has released a budget of 4500 crore rupees for this. In the first phase, work is underway to build one school each in 39 districts like Sitapur, Kanpur Dehat, Hardoi, Rae Bareli, Badaun, Gonda, Ayodhya, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Ballia, Shravasti. The target is to start admissions in these schools from March 2027. Emphasis will be on practical knowledge instead of rote learning In these schools, education will be in English medium under the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020. However, the schools will be operated under the UP Board. The plan is to emphasise practical knowledge instead of rote learning in these schools. Students in these schools will also be trained in smart classes, digital libraries, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and robotics. Separate-level labs will also be built for students from Class 1 to 12 in the school. There will be modular Math and Science labs for primary classes. Separate modern labs for Physics, Chemistry, and Biology will be established for Classes 9 to 12. Language Center: Here, students will be able to learn regional languages like Awadhi, Braj, Bundelkhandi, and Bhojpuri, in addition to English, Hindi, and Sanskrit. Pronunciation, vocabulary, and communication skills will be enhanced through audio-visual technology. AI and Robotics Training: Robotic learning centers will be established in schools, where students will be given training related to robotics, AI, and automation. Additionally, attention will be paid to coding and skill development. Mid-Day Meal: There will be a modular kitchen for approximately 1300 children from pre-primary to class 8. Here, meals will be provided under the Mid-Day Meal Scheme. Children will be able to eat in the adjacent dining hall. Safety and Health: A CCTV control center will be established within the campus to monitor approximately 1500 students studying in the school. Meanwhile, the medical room will have facilities for 2 beds, an oxygen cylinder, a stretcher, and first aid. Children will also be given training for this. Now know how to get admission The academic session of CM Composite School will start every year from April 1, but the admission process will begin in March. Admission in these schools will primarily be based on lottery or merit. Rural, economically weaker, and local children will be given priority. For this, one will have to contact the District Basic Education Officer (BSA) office or the school. The process can also be completed through an online portal. Uniform: Through DBT, money for uniform, bag, shoes, etc., will be directly credited to the bank account. Parents will be able to purchase from the market. Fees: The fee structure will be similar to Kendriya Vidyalayas or there will be a nominal fee. How different will the teachers of CM Composite Schools be? To teach in these schools, the most qualified and experienced teachers already teaching in the education department will be screened. Additionally, the responsibility for new appointments has been entrusted to the newly formed UP Education Service Selection Commission. According to the rules of Basic Education Council schools, D.El.Ed (BTC)/ B.El.Ed will be mandatory for primary level (1 to 5), and passing TET/ CTET along with B.Ed will be mandatory for upper primary and secondary level (6 to 12). Teachers must have practical knowledge of operating digital tools and smart classes. For this, they will also be given special training. Under the Central Government's 'PM SHRI' scheme, Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and other government schools are being upgraded.

stories.title: SP plans to reuse Lok Sabha strategy in 2027 election:SC candidates may contest from general seats; MLAs unlikely to lose tickets
stories.summary: As preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections gather pace, the Samajwadi Party (SP) has intensified its election planning. According to party sources, the first list of candidates has already been prepared, while work on the second list is underway. Most sitting MLAs are likely to retain their tickets in the first list. Discussions are continuing over the second list, with the party considering fielding Dalit candidates from general seats. SP is also said to be paying greater attention to reserved constituencies this time as it finalises its election strategy. Lok Sabha election formula will be adopted SP is eyeing PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak - Backward, Dalit, Minority) votes. Among these, there is a special focus on the Dalit vote bank. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP increased its tally from 5 to 37 seats, leveraging this very vote bank. If we look at the votes received by SP in 2024 assembly seat-wise, it had a lead in 184 seats. In the Lok Sabha elections, SP made a new experiment by fielding Scheduled Caste (SC) candidates on 2 general seats. Awadhesh Prasad from Faizabad and Sunita Verma from Meerut were given tickets. The result was that despite the construction of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, BJP lost the Faizabad seat. Awadhesh Prasad registered a victory by more than 50 thousand votes. Similarly, the contest in Meerut was also very close. Arun Govil, who played Ram on screen, could only win the election by 10 thousand votes. BJP was trailing in 4 out of 5 assembly seats in Meerut. If SP succeeds in making inroads into this vote bank even in 2027, its chances of returning to power will increase. SP's eye on BSP's vote bank Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says - SP will also try the formula of success achieved on Ayodhya seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the assembly elections. The party can field Dalit candidates on 40 to 50 general seats. Most of these seats will be in Western UP. Here, SP wants to win over the Dalit vote bank of BSP and Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party. This vote bank earlier belonged to BSP, but it got divided after the defeat in the 2012 assembly elections. Winning on reserved seats forms the government There are 86 reserved seats in the UP Assembly. Of these, 84 seats are reserved for SC and 2 for Scheduled Tribes (ST). In the Lok Sabha elections, 17 seats are reserved for SC in the state. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP won 7 of these seats. One seat went to Congress. The history of UP has been such that whoever wins more than half of the reserved seats forms the government in UP. A dozen leaders are demanding tickets for their families Political experts believe that SP will not cut the tickets of its current MLAs, provided they are present in the party and have a strong hold in their assembly constituency. SP currently has 102 MLAs. Many MLAs and leaders want to get tickets for their family members. These include leaders from East to West UP. Whether family members will contest the election or the current MLAs, it has not been decided yet. The number of such seats is said to be around 12.

stories.summary: A police team came under a stone-pelting attack in Ghazipur following the encounter of Kamlesh Bind, the man accused of murdering hotelier Vineet Rai. According to reports, people chased the police and hurled stones from all directions, forcing officers to run for safety. The encounter took place on Wednesday night. On Thursday, police conducted a post-mortem examination of Kamlesh Bind's body and subsequently handed it over to his family. Family members were taking the body for the final rites when they staged a protest at the Phullpur railway crossing, around 500 metres from their home. A crowd of nearly 400 people gathered at the site. Police attempt to remove body After receiving information about the protest, Circle Officer Shekhar Sengar and Sadar Kotwali Station House Officer Pramod Singh reached the spot along with around 50 male and female police personnel. When officers attempted to remove the body from the protest site, demonstrators objected and a confrontation followed. Stone-pelting forces police to flee As tensions escalated, members of the crowd allegedly began pelting stones at the police. Police personnel were forced to run in different directions to avoid the attack. Several officers reportedly took shelter inside nearby banks to protect themselves. stories.title: ‘Aamir Khan isn’t cow, buffalo that I can bring him':Brother Faisal in Hardoi says, 'Will give 2.51 lakh to the one who finds tehsildar's missing mother'
stories.summary: Film actor Faisal Khan, elder brother of Aamir Khan, visited his ancestral village in Hardoi on Thursday. During the visit, he met Tehsildar Sandhya Yadav and appealed to the public to assist in locating her mother, Lalli Devi (71), who has been missing for the past month. Faisal Khan said- Lalli Devi has been missing for the last month. The family is making continuous efforts to trace her. A reward of ₹2.51 lakh will be given to anyone who provides information about her whereabouts or helps bring her home safely. When asked why Aamir Khan had not accompanied him to the village, Faisal replied, ‘He is not a cow or buffalo that I can simply bring along. When he feels like it, he will come himself’. Family owns 120 bighas of land in the area Aamir and Faisal Khan's ancestors belonged to the Shahabad region of Hardoi district. The family owns around 120 bighas of agricultural land and orchards in Akhtiyarpur and Dilawarpur villages. Faisal Khan manages these fields and orchards. He has appeared in several films, including the movie Mela. During his visit to Hardoi, he once again appealed to people to help trace Tehsildar Sandhya Yadav's missing mother. See pictures- Know the entire matter Tehsildar Sandhya Yadav said that her mother, Lalli Devi, went to visit a temple in the Arjunganj-Ahimamau area of Lucknow on 30 April 2026. After leaving the temple, she reportedly lost her way and was unable to return home. She was last seen near the Fauji Dhaba area along the Shaheed Path service lane in Ahimamau. Since then, there has been no trace of her. The family has lodged a missing person report at Sushant Golf City Police Station. Police teams and family members have been searching for Lalli Devi continuously. The family has also launched a social media campaign and distributed posters. Search operations are being carried out in several districts. Distinctive identification mark According to Sandhya Yadav, her mother is approximately five feet tall and was last seen wearing a red saree and green bangles. The most distinctive identifying feature is a tattoo on her left hand bearing the names “Lalli Devi” and “Ramdhari”. ‘I came to look after the ancestral property’ Speaking to the media, Faisal Khan said the primary purpose of his visit was to oversee the family's ancestral agricultural land and orchards in Akhtiyarpur and Dilawarpur villages. He said he has always had an interest in farming and agriculture and now wants to take a more active role in managing the property himself. Faisal Khan also expressed support for the proposed Film City project in Uttar Pradesh. He said the project would generate new employment opportunities and provide a boost to the film industry.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan Singh’s daughter meets Surya’s mother:Says, ‘Yogi ji must break criminals’ Morale’, calls for demolition of illegal madrasas'
stories.summary: Former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's daughter, Shalini Singh, visited the home of murder victim Surya Chauhan in Ghaziabad on Thursday afternoon. She met Surya’s mother and brother, sat with them outside the house, offered condolences, and paid floral tributes to Surya. She said, ‘We have offered a job to Surya’s elder brother. Strict action will be taken against those accused in Surya’s murder. Yogiji should break the morale of criminals.’ Shalini Singh said- The government should immediately demolish illegal madrasas. How are such large illegal madrasas being constructed? They should at least produce the relevant documents. Madrasas where children are allegedly being given the wrong education should also be demolished. They are not allowing human beings to remain humane. Those who commit such heinous crimes and make videos of them, where does such a mentality come from? Who is teaching them? Tension continues in Khoda Area The Khoda area, where Surya was murdered on Bakrid, has remained tense for the past seven days. Members of various Hindu organisations have been continuously visiting Surya’s home. Police personnel have been deployed in the area to maintain security. However, around 10 to 15 per cent of shops have now reopened. Main accused killed in encounter, 5 sent to jail The main accused, Asad, was killed in a police encounter. Police have sent five accused, including Asad’s father, to jail. Surya’s mother has been given a contractual job in the Khoda Municipality by Ravindra Kumar Mandar, the District Magistrate of Ghaziabad. The state government has also provided financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to the family. See 3 pictures- Surya was allegedly called out and stabbed on Bakrid 17-year-old Surya was murdered on Bakrid (28 May). According to his minor friend, Asad called Surya to meet him. He was then allegedly surrounded by Asad and his associates and repeatedly stabbed in the stomach. Before the attack, the accused allegedly told Surya, “Have you ever seen a goat being halal? Come, we’ll show you.” CCTV footage related to the incident had also surfaced. Three more accused arrested Khoda Police arrested three more accused on Thursday afternoon. They have been identified as Asad’s father Nawab (45), Farhan (19) and Atif (19). According to police, Farhan stated during questioning that Nawab had allegedly instigated Asad to kill Surya. He is alleged to have told him: “End Surya’s story on Bakrid.”

stories.title: Hospital owner kills woman in Scorpio after rape complaint:Nude body dumped 380 km from Kanpur; wife defends accused husband
stories.summary: The owner of a prominent hospital in Unnao has been arrested for the alleged murder of a 26-year-old woman who had filed a rape case against him. Police said the accused, Devkant Uttam, called the woman for a meeting and allegedly strangled her inside a Scorpio SUV. His nephew and a security guard then transported the body nearly 380 km away and dumped it in Bulandshahr after removing her clothes to conceal her identity. The woman, who lived with her mother in Kanpur and was preparing for the Uttar Pradesh Sub-Inspector (Daroga) recruitment examination, was initially unidentified. After a post-mortem, police conducted her last rites because no one had claimed the body. Mother’s complaint led police to the accused When the woman failed to return home, her mother lodged a complaint against Devkant Uttam and his nephew at Barra police station in Kanpur. During the investigation, the nephew allegedly stabbed himself in the stomach in an attempt to mislead police. He was taken into custody after being discharged from hospital on May 30. During questioning, he allegedly confessed to the murder and revealed how the body had been disposed of. Following the confession, police identified the victim and linked the case to the accused hospital owner. Devkant Uttam later surrendered before police. Before surrendering, he released a video claiming he was innocent. Police formally disclosed details of the case on Wednesday. Security guard Ajit Singh has also been arrested. Police: Accused lured woman, recorded photos and videos According to investigators, the accused first met the woman when she visited his hospital in Unnao for treatment in February 2024. Police said he obtained her phone number and later contacted her regularly, promising to marry her. The two allegedly developed a relationship, and Uttam took her to Madhya Pradesh, where he had sexual relations with her and recorded objectionable photos and videos. Police said the woman later became pregnant and was allegedly forced to undergo an abortion in August 2025. When the woman pressed for marriage, the accused allegedly refused. Police said he then threatened to release her private photos and videos. Distressed by the threats, she filed a rape complaint against him on May 19. Murder allegedly planned after rape FIR Police said the rape complaint angered the accused, who then conspired to kill the woman. On May 21, he allegedly called her to meet him near Barra Bypass in Kanpur. His nephew Vivek Patel was also present in the Scorpio SUV. Investigators said the woman was strangled to death shortly after she got into the vehicle. The body was then taken to the accused's under-construction hospital in Unnao. From there, Vivek Patel and security guard Ajit Singh allegedly transported it to Bulandshahr via the Ganga Expressway. Body dumped in orchard, identity hidden According to police, the accused removed the victim’s clothes and abandoned the body in a mango orchard near Anupshahr Highway in Bulandshahr on the night of May 22. Investigators said they attempted to conceal her identity but overlooked a sacred thread tied to her wrist and a nose stud. The body was recovered by Bulandshahr police on May 23. As her identity remained unknown, police conducted her cremation on May 24 after completing post-mortem formalities. Later, the victim’s mother identified her from photographs using the sacred thread and nose stud. Accused linked to politics, planned Assembly bid Police said Devkant Uttam is associated with the BJP and was preparing to contest the Assembly election from the Jahanabad constituency in Fatehpur district. He also operates a hospital in Unnao and was constructing another medical facility in the district. Investigators added that his father died shortly before his arrest. Victim had filed another rape case Police investigation also found that the woman had filed a separate rape case on May 19 against a property dealer from Kanpur Dehat. She alleged that she was sexually assaulted after being given an intoxicating substance in January 2025. Based on her complaint, the accused property dealer was arrested and sent to jail, where he remains lodged. Wife claims husband is innocent Devkant Uttam’s wife has defended him, claiming he has been falsely implicated. She alleged that the woman used to trap people and extort money, a claim that has not been substantiated by investigators. Police said the murder investigation is continuing and further legal action will be taken based on evidence collected during the probe.

stories.title: 2 land dealers' bodies found near college in Varanasi:Police launch probe with murder angle, poisonous material was found at scene
stories.summary: Two young men involved in land business in Varanasi were found dead under suspicious circumstances. Their bodies were found lying near the boundary behind Harishchandra Degree College in Baniyapur. It is being suspected that both young men were murdered and their bodies were brought and dumped here. Upon receiving information, police and forensic team reached the spot and started investigation. College staff spotted two bodies In the morning, when college staff reached the premises, they saw two bodies lying near the boundary. When police arrived after receiving information, a crowd of nearby villagers gathered. Police cordoned off the area and took it under their control and started collecting evidence. It has also come to light that a suspicious poisonous substance was found at the scene, which is being investigated. Both were involved in land business In the preliminary investigation, the deceased have been identified as Abhijit Ganguly, a resident of Nai Basti in Hukulgunj, and Nihal Singh, a resident of Kohasi in Cholapur. Both were associated with land business. According to the police, both had gone to see a relative's land. What happened to them after that has not yet been clarified. The police are investigating various angles to determine the motive behind the murder. Foul smell was emanating from the bodies According to police officials, both bodies appear to be old and a strong foul smell was coming from them. This raises suspicion that the deaths may have occurred one or two days ago. However, the exact time and cause of death will only be clear after the postmortem report arrives. DCP, ACP reached the spot As soon as information about the incident was received, DCP Varuna Pramod Kumar, ACP Sarnath Vidush Saxena, SO Cholapur and SOG team reached the spot. The officers inspected the scene and directed the forensic team to collect evidence. Police have taken both bodies into custody and after completing the panchnama, sent them for post-mortem. The relatives of the deceased have also reached the spot and are being questioned. Police investigating several points Police are trying to find out who the two youths were last in contact with and how they reached the scene. People in the vicinity are being questioned. Along with this, mobile call details and other technical evidence are also being examined.

stories.title: Inspector found hanging from window in Badaun:Body discovered in kneeling position, suicide suspected
stories.summary: A police inspector posted in court security was found hanging inside his rented room in Badaun on Thursday morning. The body was discovered hanging from a noose tied to the ventilator grill above the room's door. The inspector was found in a kneeling position. No suicide note was recovered from the scene. Superintendent of Police Ankita Sharma said the case appears to be a suicide prima facie, but the exact circumstances will be confirmed only after the post-mortem report and further investigation. Inspector had been living in the house for a year The deceased, Inspector Meghshyam Gautam (55), was posted in court security. He was a native of Sakna village in the Govindnagar police station area of Mathura and had been living in a rented room in Madhuban Colony under Nagar Kotwali police station limits for the past year. Police have seized his mobile phone and are examining call records. A forensic team also inspected the scene. See pictures- Daughter alerted landlord after calls went unanswered Landlord Vikesh said he owns a two-storey house and that Gautam lived on the first floor along with two other families. According to Vikesh, he was in his village when Gautam's daughter called him at around 9 am on Thursday. She said she had been trying to contact her father repeatedly but was unable to reach him. Vikesh informed his wife, who knocked on Gautam's door several times but received no response. He then returned home and informed the police. When police arrived and broke open the door, they found Gautam hanging inside the room. SP: Situation will become clear after post-mortem, family questioning SP Ankita Sharma said police received information at around 9:45 am about the incident. The body was found hanging from a noose made with a towel tied to the ventilator grill above the 6.5-foot-high door. "No suicide note has been found. The mobile phone has been seized and call details are being examined. The exact circumstances will become clear after questioning family members and receiving the post-mortem report," she said.

stories.title: UP govt transfers 206 police officers:Stuti Singh posted as Sambhal CO; Vikas Jaiswal joins CM security, Kannauj DSP Priyanka shifted to Kanpur
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government on Thursday transferred 206 Provincial Police Service (PPS) officers in a major administrative reshuffle. The transfers include a large number of officers who had been posted at the same station for an extended period, as well as several officers recently promoted from inspector to Circle Officer (CO). Deputy Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar-II, who was serving in the Chief Minister’s security detail, has been transferred to Shahjahanpur. Lucknow Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vikas Kumar Jaiswal has been assigned to the Chief Minister’s security unit. The transfer of ACP Arvind Kumar-II from the Gautam Buddha Nagar Commissionerate to Lakhimpur Kheri has been cancelled, allowing him to continue in his current posting. Among other key transfers, Kannauj DSP Priyanka Bajpai has been posted as ACP in Kanpur, while Bijnor DSP Som Prakash Verma has been transferred to Mau. Agra ACP Sukanya Sharma has been appointed DSP of Baghpat, and Hapur DSP Stuti Singh has been posted as CO Sambhal. Lucknow ACP Satish Kumar Rai has been transferred to the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) in Meerut. Rajeev Kumar Sisodia, CO of Railway Saharanpur, and Dr Ravi Shankar, CO of Muzaffarnagar, have been posted as ACPs in the Gautam Buddha Nagar Commissionerate. CM security gets new officer Deputy Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar-II, who was posted in the Chief Minister's security wing in Lucknow, has been transferred to Shahjahanpur. In his place, CO Vikas Kumar Jaiswal from Raebareli has been given the responsibility of the Chief Minister's security. In another decision, the government cancelled the transfer of ACP Arvind Kumar-II from Gautam Buddh Nagar Commissionerate to Kheri. He will continue in his current posting. Major changes in Lucknow and Noida commissionerates In Lucknow Commissionerate, Uday Pratap Singh-II from Gorakhpur, Rajesh Kumar Singh from Agra and Abhishek Kumar Pandey from Kanpur Nagar have been appointed as new ACPs. ACP Satish Kumar Rai has been transferred from Lucknow to PAC Meerut. In Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida) Commissionerate, Rajiv Kumar Sisodiya from Railway Saharanpur and Dr Ravi Shankar from Muzaffarnagar have been posted as ACPs. Key transfers across districts and units Among the notable transfers, Anuruddh Kumar has been moved from Maharajganj to Mahoba, Abhishek Singh from Kaushambi to Balrampur, Ajay Kumar Shrotiya from Jhansi to Amroha and Pankaj Pant from Shahjahanpur to Rampur. Ashok Kumar Mishra-II has been shifted from Bhadohi to the 30th Battalion PAC in Gonda, while Manish Kumar Yadav has been transferred from Prayagraj Airport Security to the 4th Battalion PAC in Prayagraj. Several officers have also been posted to Varanasi Commissionerate, PAC battalions, LIU units and police training centres across the state. Women officers receive new postings The reshuffle also changed the jurisdictions of several women officers. Stuti Singh has been transferred from Hapur to Sambhal. Sarjana Singh has been moved from Aligarh and posted as Assistant Commandant of the 49th Battalion PAC in Gautam Buddh Nagar. Jyotishree has been transferred from Balrampur and appointed ACP in Kanpur Nagar Commissionerate. Shweta Verma has been posted as ACP in Agra Commissionerate from Mathura. Vineeta has been shifted from Hamirpur to Police Training School (PTS), Meerut. Shuchita Singh has been appointed ACP in Ghaziabad Commissionerate from Meerut. Immediate joining ordered The DGP Headquarters has directed all 206 transferred officers to immediately hand over charge and join their new postings. The order aims to ensure a smooth transition and prevent any disruption to law and order duties across the state. See the complete list...

stories.title: TGT exam enters second day in Gorakhpur:Candidates screened with metal detectors, over 18,000 set to appear
stories.summary: The second day of the Uttar Pradesh Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) Recruitment Examination began on Thursday amid tight security arrangements across examination centres in Gorakhpur. Entry for the first shift started early in the morning, with candidates being allowed inside only after multiple levels of verification. Officials conducted screening through metal detectors, Aadhaar card verification and retina scans before permitting candidates to take their seats. Candidates were also seen checking their examination rooms and roll numbers outside the centres before entering. 15 centres in first shift, 24 in second A total of 15 examination centres have been set up for the first shift, while the second shift will be conducted at 24 centres across the city. Altogether, 18,188 candidates have registered for the examination on the second day. The first day's examination on Wednesday was completed peacefully without any disruption. Recruitment exam being held after four years The recruitment examination is being conducted after nearly four years and has attracted candidates from across Uttar Pradesh. The district administration and education department have made extensive arrangements to ensure smooth conduct of the examination. According to data released by the commission, 868,531 candidates have applied for 3,539 teaching posts. The examination is being held over two days, June 3 and 4, 2026. Documents required for entry Candidates must carry the following documents to the examination centre: Officials said candidates without the required documents could face difficulties in appearing for the examination. No negative marking The commission has confirmed that there will be no negative marking in the examination. As a result, candidates can attempt all questions without the risk of losing marks for incorrect answers. OMR sheets to be handled by invigilators Candidates will not be required to separate the copy of their OMR answer sheet after the examination. Invigilators will separate the answer sheet copy and hand it over to candidates. Gates to close 45 minutes before exam The commission has issued strict instructions regarding entry timings. No candidate will be allowed to enter the examination centre after the gates are closed. Tight security arrangements at all centres Authorities have strengthened security measures at all examination centres to ensure fair and peaceful conduct of the recruitment test. Special monitoring teams have also been deployed. Officials have advised candidates to follow all examination guidelines carefully and reach their centres well before the reporting time to avoid any inconvenience.

stories.title: Lucknow shines in IIRF 2026 rankings:IIM placed 5th, BBAU 19th; Law faculty secures 13th rank nationally
stories.summary: Lucknow's Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University (BBAU) has secured the 19th rank among Central Universities in the Indian Institutional Ranking Framework (IIRF) 2026. The university's Department of Law also performed strongly, securing the 13th position at the national level. Meanwhile, IIM Lucknow was ranked fifth among management institutes in India. IIM Lucknow slips to fifth rank In the IIRF 2026 rankings, IIM Lucknow dropped one place from last year and secured the fifth position nationwide. The institute scored 94.74 points based on parameters such as research output, placements, alumni feedback, graduate outcomes, and employability. In the 2025 rankings, IIM Lucknow had secured the fourth rank. IIM Lucknow Director Prof. M.P. Gupta said the achievement reflects the collective efforts of the institute's faculty, students, alumni, staff, and industry partners. He said the institute remains committed to promoting quality management education, research, innovation, social responsibility, and leadership development. Vice Chancellor congratulates university community BBAU Vice Chancellor Prof. Raj Kumar Mittal congratulated the university's teachers, staff, and students on the achievement. He said the ranking is the result of the combined efforts of the entire university community and expressed confidence that BBAU will continue to achieve greater success at both national and international levels. Established in 1996 Established in 1996, BBAU is one of the country's leading central universities. The institution offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programmes through its campuses in Lucknow and Amethi. Focus on research, innovation and inclusion The Vice Chancellor said the university remains focused on promoting quality education, research, innovation, and social inclusion. He added that these efforts have helped BBAU improve its performance in national rankings and strengthen its appeal among students across the country.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Noida, trees uprooted:Roads waterlogged; storm hits Aligarh as rain sweeps 12 cities in UP
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has been witnessing spells of storms and rain for the past 10 days. In Noida, dense clouds covered the sky at around 2 pm on Thursday, plunging the city into darkness during the daytime. According to the Meteorological Department, winds gusting up to 93 kmph were recorded. Around 12 mm of rainfall fell within an hour. Waterlogging of up to one foot was reported in several areas. In Film City, uprooted trees fell onto parked vehicles. Rain and strong winds affect several districts Sambhal received rain following strong winds, while Aligarh reported considerable damage due to the storm and rainfall. Ghaziabad witnessed a dust storm, and rain was reported in 12 cities, including Ayodhya and Meerut. A storm and rainfall alert has been issued for 42 districts on Thursday. Meteorologists have said that the monsoon is expected to enter Uttar Pradesh through the Gorakhpur region by 18 June and reach Lucknow by 22 June. Rainfall far below forecast On Wednesday, districts including Kanpur, Gorakhpur and Azamgarh recorded only 0.2 mm of rainfall. This was 87 per cent below the forecast, as meteorologists had predicted around 1.2 mm of rainfall. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- A new western disturbance is active over north-west India. Due to its influence, scattered rainfall is likely across western and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Hailstorms are also possible. Winds may reach speeds of up to 70 kmph. Similar weather conditions are expected to continue over the next three days. See weather related pictures- Weather forecast for the next five days 5 June- Cloud cover is expected across the state. Light rain may occur in some places. Temperatures are unlikely to fall significantly, but relief from heatwave conditions will continue. 6 June- Light rainfall is likely in most districts. Humidity levels will remain high, keeping temperatures largely stable. No heatwave conditions are expected. 7 June- Light rain is forecast across the state. Periods of bright sunshine may occur between showers, which could increase humidity and discomfort. 8 June- Weather conditions are expected to remain clear across Uttar Pradesh. Strong sunshine is likely, and no rainfall is forecast. 9 June- Most districts are expected to experience bright sunshine. Winds of up to 30 kmph may blow across the state, providing some relief from humid conditions.

stories.title: UP police reshuffle on cards:Renuka Mishra in line for DG Vigilance; two commissioners may be shifted
stories.summary: After the permanent appointment of DGP Rajeev Krishna, there were expectations that long-pending police postings would be cleared quickly. However, the transfer list remains on hold, with appointments to several senior posts, including DG, ADG and IG, yet to be finalised. According to sources, administrative factors have slowed the process. With Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath closely monitoring law and order, action against several SSPs and Police Commissioners is also being considered. The May 31 order confirming Rajeev Krishna as DGP did not mention the additional charge of the Vigilance Department that he had been holding. As a result, the DG Vigilance post is now technically vacant. DG Rules Manual post under discussion DG Rules Manual Antony Dev Kumar retired on May 31. Within the police department, the post is often viewed as a non-field assignment. Antony Dev Kumar, who was promoted from ADG to DG in March 2026, was nearing retirement and was therefore not given a major field posting. Renuka Mishra may be adjusted to vacant post There is speculation that 1990-batch IPS officer Renuka Mishra could be posted as DG Rules Manual. She is the senior-most IPS officer in Uttar Pradesh and was considered a contender for the DGP post. However, her prospects were affected by the constable recruitment paper leak controversy. In its report to the UPSC, the state government stated that a blacklisted company was awarded the paper-printing contract during her tenure as recruitment board chairperson. Following the controversy, she was attached to the DGP headquarters. Several senior posts await appointments CM reviews law and order performance Sources say the delay in the transfer list is also linked to the Chief Minister's review of recent law and order incidents. Officials believe changes in at least two police commissionerates and two district police units are likely in the next transfer order.

stories.title: 4 murders, ₹1.5 crore loot, and a deadly betrayal:Friend-turned-killer stayed with bodies for 12 hours; son's attack shattered father's skull into 10 pieces
stories.summary: Sunny Gupta, accused of killing four members of a wealthy businessman's family in Prayagraj, allegedly spent nearly 12 hours inside the house after the murders, trying to erase evidence before leaving. According to police, Sunny left the house around 5 am on June 1 and reached his home by 6:30 am. When family members questioned him about being away all night, he claimed he had been preparing kachoris for a wedding. He then went to his room and slept. To trace the accused, police scanned footage from nearly 150 CCTV cameras within a 2-km radius. One camera captured Sunny leaving the businessman's house. Investigators showed the footage to a kachori-samosa vendor operating near the residence, who identified him. Based on this lead, police arrested Sunny, who later confessed during questioning. Police also recovered jewellery worth about Rs 1.5 crore, allegedly looted from the house of businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya. The postmortem report, received on June 3, revealed that Abhishek and his friend Sunny Gupta first killed Abhishek's sister. One bone in her skull was found fractured. They then allegedly murdered Abhishek's parents, with around 10 skull fractures found on each of them. Investigators said Sunny later killed Abhishek as well and allegedly poured toilet cleaner on his face in an attempt to destroy evidence. The postmortem found 12 injury marks on Abhishek's body. Meanwhile, two police inspectors have been suspended for alleged negligence in connection with the case. Police scanned 150 CCTV cameras to trace accused Investigators examined footage from nearly 150 CCTV cameras across a 2-km radius, from South Malaka to Mahaviran Gali, to crack the quadruple murder case. One camera captured accused Sunny Gupta leaving businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya's house around 5 am on June 1. Further analysis showed Sunny entering the house with Vaishya's son Abhishek around 3 pm on May 31. Another footage later showed him returning to his home in Mutthiganj after leaving the Vaishya residence. Brother had reported him missing Sunny's family grew concerned when he failed to return home on the night of May 31 and his mobile phone remained switched off. His brother Manoj informed South Malaka police station that Sunny was missing, but no immediate action was taken. When Sunny returned home on June 1, his brother asked where he had been. Sunny claimed he had spent the night preparing kachoris at a wedding and would earn Rs 5,000 for the work. He then went to sleep. Postmortem reveals brutal killings The postmortem of businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya, his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi and son Abhishek was conducted on June 3. According to the report, Abhishek and Sunny first attacked Meenakshi, leaving a skull fracture. They then killed Virendra and Anita, repeatedly striking their heads with an iron rod. Doctors found multiple fractures in both victims' skulls. Police said Sunny later turned on Abhishek and killed him with the same weapon. The postmortem found several fractures and injury marks on his chest, arms, legs and face. Investigators said Sunny poured toilet cleaner on Abhishek's face and later attempted to erase evidence by cleaning blood stains inside the house. He reportedly stayed in the house overnight, bathed there and left around 5 am on June 1. Now read what came in the postmortem report On June 3, the postmortem of Virendra Kumar Vaishya, his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi, and son Abhishek was conducted. According to the report, Abhishek brutally killed his parents. He struck their heads more than 12 times. This shattered the front, back, and middle bones of both their skulls. Meanwhile, sister Meenakshi was found with only one front bone broken. After the 3 murders, Sunny Gupta also brutally killed Abhishek. He struck Abhishek repeatedly with an iron rod. This resulted in his skull bones also being broken. Additionally, injuries were found on his chest, arms, legs, and face. After committing the murders, Sunny poured toilet cleaner on Abhishek's face. This caused his face to be scorched. After the 4 murders, Sunny cleaned the blood stains from the stairs and rooms. He bathed in the bathroom. After this, he slept in the house itself. About 12 hours later, he left the businessman's house around 5 AM on the morning of June 1. Police Commissioner suspends two officers The investigation has also revealed alleged negligence by police. On the night of May 31, Sunny Gupta's brother informed police that he was missing and his phone was switched off. Officials later found lapses in the response to the information. Following the inquiry, Police Commissioner Jogendra Kumar suspended South Malaka outpost in-charge Rohit Kumar Gaud and Senior Sub-Inspector Mulayam Yadav of Kotwali police station. The case at a glance Virendra Kumar Vaishya ran a gift business and lived with his family in a two-storey house at Heewet Road crossing in Prayagraj. The 8,000 sq ft property, estimated to be worth Rs 10-15 crore, has 14 shops on the ground floor, 13 of which are rented out. Virendra lived on the upper floor with his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi and son Abhishek. Meenakshi managed a gift shop in the building, while Abhishek dealt in pesticides and floor-cleaning products. Both siblings were unmarried. The couple's younger son, Ashwini, is lodged in Kaushambi jail. His wife Ritu is currently out on bail and staying at her parental home in Kidganj. On June 2, the bodies of Virendra (70), Anita (65) and Meenakshi (45) were found inside the locked house. Around two hours later, the body of Abhishek (40) was recovered from a shop on the ground floor. That shop was also locked from outside. Abhishek often clashed with his father Police said Abhishek had a strained relationship with his father. Neighbours and relatives told investigators that disputes over money and business matters were common in the family. According to the probe, Abhishek had previously borrowed several lakh rupees and failed to repay the amount on time. The lender allegedly assaulted him and threatened the family. His sister Meenakshi later arranged the money and secured his release, leading to further tensions between Abhishek and his father. A mansion left without an heir The Vaishya family's wealth included a prime 8,000 sq ft property and 14 shops generating rental income worth several lakh rupees every month. With Virendra, Anita, Meenakshi and Abhishek dead, and the younger son in jail, there is currently no immediate family member living in the house. Police reconstruction of the crime Six questions that still remain unanswered Despite the police explanation, several questions continue to raise doubts.

stories.title: 21 UP highways set for four-lane upgrade:Speed limit to rise from 80 to 100 kmph; major boost for East UP
stories.summary: 21 state highways in UP will become four-lane. This work will be completed by December 2027. The Public Works Department has completed the survey of these roads passing through 18 districts. The proposal has been sent to the state government. The state government is improving state highways along with expressways and national highways. There are 142 state highways in UP. 107 state highways have been widened up to 10 meters. In the second phase, 21 state highways are being made four-lane. After this work is completed, the remaining 14 state highways will also be made four-lane. On these four-lane highways, vehicles will run at a maximum speed of 90-100 km. Earlier they used to run at a speed of 70-80 km. Now the journey will not only be comfortable, but will also be completed quickly. 3 state highways of Varanasi, 2 of Hardoi will be developed Among the 21 state highways in the state, 3 roads from Varanasi and 2 from Hardoi are included. Apart from this, roads from Amethi, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Deoria, Kushinagar, Jalaun, Farrukhabad, Lucknow, Moradabad, Bulandshahr, Meerut, Sonbhadra, Sambhal, Muzaffarnagar, Chandauli and Jaunpur have been included. In this way, around 18 districts are going to benefit. Here the roads are 7 to 14 meters wide, but now they will be widened from 14 to 25 meters. First, know about the 9 roads that will become four-lane... Jagdishpur Road- This 28-kilometer long road connects Amethi to Sultanpur, Pratapgarh and Raebareli. 639 crore rupees will be spent on its widening. Bahraich-Bhinga-Sirsia-Chaudhary Deeh Road- About 21 kilometers of road will be widened. 46 crore rupees will be spent on this. Deoria-Padrauna Highway- This 31-kilometer road will be made four-lane for better connectivity to Kushinagar International Airport and Agricultural University. 292 crores will be spent on this. Panwari Highway (Jalaun)- This road is 53 kilometers long. Work on this road started 10 years ago. After some portion was built, the work stopped. Now 223 crores will be spent to complete it. Bilgram-Unnao-Prayagraj Route- The length of this road is 90 kilometers. Preparations are underway to upgrade it to a National Highway. 5442 crore rupees will be spent. BSA State Highway in Hardoi- More road accidents occur on this highway. About 67 crore rupees are being spent on this approximately 11 kilometer long route. Its construction is ongoing. Three Routes in Varanasi- Chaubeypur Road, Varanasi-Kachwa Road and Kachwa-Chaubeypur Road are being made four-lane. PWD has not made public how much budget is being spent on this. Four-lane highway will have many hi-tech facilities Four-lane roads are designed in such a way that the speed of vehicles remains at 90 to 100 km/hour. This will make the journey comfortable. Bikes can also run on these. Their high speed remains 80-90 km/hour. Compared to normal 2-lane roads, many modern facilities are provided on four-lane roads. These are different based on safety and infrastructure. Know these too... Rumble strips will wake up sleeping drivers Safe Divider- There is a divider in the middle to separate traffic from both sides. Plants are grown on it, so that at night the headlight beams from oncoming vehicles do not fall on the eyes. Crash Barrier- There are strong barriers made of steel or concrete on the sides of the road and on the divider. This prevents any vehicle from going out of control and falling off the road or going to the other side. Rumble Strips- White colored raised strips are made on the road before toll plazas, junctions or accidental zones. These cause vibrations in vehicles, which wake up sleeping drivers. Reflectors- Reflective reflectors are installed in the middle and on the sides of the road to show the way at night or during fog. Service Lane for Local Traffic Service Road- A separate service lane is provided for local traffic of villages or towns situated along the highway. This ensures that local vehicles do not disturb the speed of the main highway. Underpass and Overpass- Underpasses are constructed for local residents, animals, and vehicles to cross from one side to the other. This eliminates the risk of accidents on the highway. Bypass- To avoid traffic jams in big cities, a bypass is created outside the cities. Drainage System- To prevent rainwater from accumulating on the road, paved drains are built on both sides. This prevents the road from deteriorating quickly. Parking for Trucks Truck Parking- To prevent trucks from parking on the roadside, separate large parking spaces are created. These have facilities for toilets and rest rooms. Petrol Pump, Restaurant- For travelers, petrol pumps, restaurants, dhabas, toilets, and vehicle repair shops are developed at fixed distances. Help Available Every 2 km in Case of Accident Emergency Calling Box- In case of any accident or vehicle breakdown, SOS boxes or helpline numbers are provided every 1-2 kilometers for assistance. Ambulance and Crane Service- In case of toll roads, the highway authority's quick response team, ambulances, and patrolling vehicles continuously make rounds. Smart Sign Boards- Reflective sign boards are installed that provide information about speed limits, upcoming turns, and routes.

stories.title: Lucknow man kills younger brother, smashes head with cylinder:Drags body onto street after attack, dumps body outside, challenges onlookers
stories.summary: In Lucknow, an elder brother allegedly murdered his younger brother after the latter objected to him assaulting their parents. The accused repeatedly struck his brother on the head with a domestic LPG cylinder. He then dragged the blood-soaked victim by the leg and dumped him on the road. Shouting at bystanders, he allegedly said, “I have killed him. Let anyone do whatever they want now.” The victim’s uncle and local residents rushed him to the Trauma Centre, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 3 pm on Sunday in Sector-3 of Jankipuram Extension. The deceased, Aryan Mishra (21), worked at a seed warehouse. Police have taken the accused elder brother, Abhishek Mishra (24), into custody. First 2 pictures Now the complete incident in detail Father said - he often used to assault in a state of intoxication Aryan’s father, Ramanand Mishra, works as a painting contractor. He said that his younger son Aryan worked in medicine supply at a seed warehouse in Daliganj, while his elder son Abhishek was unemployed. According to Ramanand, Abhishek frequently assaulted family members after consuming intoxicants. On Sunday morning, he first attacked him. The family somehow managed to escape and took shelter on the rooftop. Later, Ramanand and his wife prepared to leave for Yahiyaganj to purchase goods for their shop. During this time, Abhishek allegedly started beating his mother, Manju Mishra. He kicked her on the road. Local residents intervened and tried to stop him. When Aryan objected to the assault, Abhishek abused him and then attacked him with the gas cylinder. Both brothers first fought on the road Neighbour Shiv Poojan Mishra said that after the morning dispute, Ramanand left with his wife. However, the argument between the two brothers continued. A serious fight broke out on the road. Tenants living nearby and other residents intervened and separated the brothers. Abhishek was sent inside the house, while Aryan was taken into a neighbouring house adjoining their residence. However, Aryan later returned to Abhishek through the rooftop route, where another heated argument broke out between them. The neighbour said Abhishek was extremely aggressive during the confrontation. 'Abhishek was bloodthirsty' Abhishek allegedly struck Aryan on the head with the LPG cylinder, leaving him covered in blood and collapsing to the ground. Even then, his anger did not subside. He grabbed Aryan by the leg and dragged him onto the road. He then reportedly told residents, “I have killed him. Now do whatever you want.” Following the attack, Aryan’s uncle Parmanand, with the help of local residents, rushed him to the Trauma Centre in critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. Blood spread on the road Local residents said Aryan’s head had suffered severe injuries. He lay inside the house, drenched in blood and struggling for life. Blood had spread from inside the house onto the road outside. Police and forensic experts reached the scene and collected evidence as part of the investigation.
