stories.title: 2-storey mosque demolished with bulldozer in Sambhal:55-foot minaret pulled down with crane; ‘I Love Mohammad’ posters found
stories.summary: A mosque named Mustafa Qadri, allegedly built on government cemetery land in Sambhal, was demolished using bulldozers on Saturday. The mosque, located in Kaserua village of the Nakhasa area, was first dismantled from the front portion and pillars before its 55-foot-high minaret was brought down using a hydra machine. The District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police were present at the site during the demolition drive. Officials recovered posters bearing the words “I Love Mohammad” and a green flag from the mosque’s first floor. The SP said action would be taken against those responsible for printing and displaying such posters. The demolition was carried out following an order from the Tehsildar Court, which directed the removal of encroachment from around 120 square metres of government land. Four bulldozers, dumpers, tractors and 20 sanitation workers from Sirsi Nagar Panchayat were deployed for the operation. Before the action began, members of the Muslim community offered prayers at the mosque. The administration then removed glass panels and gates. Police also evacuated houses around the mosque premises. More than 100 police personnel were deployed in the village to maintain law and order. See 5 pictures... Read the full matter The Tehsildar Court had passed an eviction order against the mosque committee on April 21. The committee later appealed in the District Magistrate’s court, but no stay order or relief was granted. Following this, the administration decided to proceed with the demolition. Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh constituted a special team for the operation and appointed Naib Tehsildar Deepak Kumar Jurail as the campaign in-charge. The revenue department sought four JCB machines, dumpers, tractors and 20 sanitation workers from Sambhal Municipality and Sirsi Nagar Panchayat. According to revenue records, plot number 409 is designated as cemetery land. The administration claims that the mosque had been constructed on nearly 120 square metres of this land. Three residential houses were also allegedly built on the same plot. Officials further stated that plot number 410, recorded as land reserved for manure pits, had around 600 square metres occupied by eight houses. Part of plot number 411, reserved for plantation, was also allegedly being used for cultivation. Around 1,000 people offered prayers at the mosque Mosque caretaker Zakir Hussain said the mosque dates back several generations and was rebuilt around 20–25 years ago at a cost exceeding ₹50 lakh. Villagers alleged that their side was not properly heard during proceedings in the Tehsildar Court. Local resident Javed said they received no prior information about the demolition and only learned about it on Saturday morning. He claimed the mosque was older than previous land consolidation exercises and had been used by local families for generations. He added that around 1,000 people offered Friday prayers at the two-storey mosque and that the village population itself was close to 1,000. Action will be taken against those who printed posters - SP Mosque committee could not provide evidence Tehsildar Dhirendra Kumar Singh said villagers had filed complaints seeking protection of cemetery land. During the inquiry, officials found that the mosque had been built on cemetery land, leading to proceedings under Section 67 of the Revenue Code. He said the mosque committee was given full opportunity to present its case but failed to produce any document or evidence proving that the structure stood on private land. The court subsequently issued an eviction order. For the operation, police personnel from several stations, including Nakhasa, Kailadevi and Raysatti, were deployed along with women police officers and 60 PAC personnel. FIR was registered earlier as well In January 2026, an FIR was registered against seven individuals based on a complaint by a revenue official. They were accused of submitting incorrect documents and facts in an attempt to have the land declared Waqf property and of illegally occupying village community land. Sambhal has witnessed several anti-encroachment drives on government land in recent months. Last year, authorities cleared encroachments in the Sher Khan Sarai area, while on June 5 an alleged illegal religious structure built on government land in Baghau village of Gunnaur was also removed. stories.title: Man fires 10 rounds, pushes police officer in Mathura:Cop warns, ‘Put the gun down before someone gets shot’
stories.summary: A dramatic half-hour standoff unfolded on a Mathura road between a local strongman carrying a licensed revolver and a police officer who tried to disarm him. When the officer attempted to seize the weapon, the accused resisted, pushing and shoving him, issuing threats and engaging in a scuffle. The officer repeatedly warned him to put the gun down, saying it could accidentally go off. However, the accused refused to comply. After considerable effort, police finally managed to overpower him. The incident took place in Krishna Nagar, one of Mathura’s busiest and most affluent areas frequented by tourists. A large crowd gathered at the scene, causing a lengthy traffic jam on both sides of the road. Earlier, the accused had allegedly fired multiple rounds from his licensed revolver at Bhuteshwar Akhada. According to eyewitnesses, he arrived at the wrestling arena in a white Scorpio SUV on Friday night and opened fire immediately after stepping out of the vehicle. Panic spread through the area as people ran for safety. Hearing the gunshots and screams, local residents and wrestlers from the akhada rushed to the spot and informed the police. Before officers could arrive, the accused abandoned his vehicle and fled on foot while carrying the revolver. Frightened by the sight of an armed man running through the streets, people hid wherever they could. Police chased him for nearly a kilometre before finally catching him. Six empty cartridge cases were recovered from the accused. Police are examining video footage and CCTV recordings as part of the investigation. The incident took place around 9 pm in the Kotwali police station area. 3 Pictures- Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- Accused clashes with police on busy road Police intercepted the accused nearly one kilometre away in the Krishna Nagar area. He reportedly stood in the middle of the road holding the revolver, causing panic among bystanders. When officers asked him to hand over the weapon, he allegedly began threatening them and refused to cooperate. He then got into a scuffle with Krishna Nagar outpost in-charge Sanjeev Kumar and Sub-Inspector Mustaq Mohammad Mehndi. Police eventually dragged him to the roadside and forcibly seized the revolver. During a search, officers also recovered empty cartridge cases from his possession. The accused remains in custody and is being questioned. Six empty cartridge cases were recovered from the scene.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries at BHU rise 35-fold since 2018:Over 34,000 patients treated under scheme; beneficiaries from Bihar and Jharkhand also seek care
stories.summary: The number of patients receiving treatment under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme at Sir Sundarlal Hospital of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has increased significantly since the scheme was launched in 2018. According to data released by the university administration, the number of beneficiaries has risen nearly 35-fold over the years. Apart from Uttar Pradesh, a large number of patients from Bihar and Jharkhand are also receiving treatment at the hospital. Dr Rajeev, Medical Superintendent of BHU, said Sir Sundarlal Hospital is often referred to as the "AIIMS of Purvanchal" and treats more than 10,000 patients every day. He said cancer, heart disease, diabetes and other medicine-related ailments account for the largest share of patients receiving treatment under the scheme. Since 2018, a total of 34,363 patients have availed treatment benefits under Ayushman Bharat at the hospital. Bihar payment delays raised with Centre A dispute over delayed payments for Bihar patients treated under the scheme surfaced earlier this year. On February 5, concerns were raised that the Bihar government was not releasing payments for treatment costs on time. Following the issue, the BHU administration wrote to the Union Health Ministry seeking intervention. Buxar MP Sudhakar Singh also wrote to the Bihar Chief Minister, expressing concern over nearly ₹8 crore in pending dues for the treatment of Bihar patients at the hospital's Trauma Centre. Pending dues now being cleared Dr Rajeev said the pending payments have now started arriving, ensuring that patient treatment continues without any hurdles. He said the hospital never stopped treating patients despite delays in reimbursements. No patient was denied treatment, provided their documents were complete. Nearly 15,000 patients treated in last two years According to BHU administration data, 14,912 patients received treatment under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme at the hospital during the past two years. The beneficiaries included: Hospital officials said the scheme has helped thousands of economically weaker patients access specialised treatment that would otherwise be difficult to afford. Centre and states share scheme costs Ayushman Bharat is jointly funded by the Central and State governments. In most states, the Centre and states share the cost in a 60:40 ratio. For northeastern and Himalayan states, the funding pattern is 90:10. In Union Territories without legislative assemblies, the Central government bears the entire cost of the scheme.

stories.title: Dimple Chaudhary shares another video of man attempting to misbehave:Haryanvi dancer touched inappropriately in Hathras; demands justice
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary has released a second video showing alleged misbehaviour during a stage performance in Hathras, Uttar Pradesh. The footage appears to show a young man crossing the barricade and attempting to touch her inappropriately while she was performing. Reacting to the incident, Dimple said she has been facing questions from family members and society ever since the video surfaced. She said she was forced to switch off her phone and has been mentally distressed and uncomfortable for several days. “I want justice,” she said. The incident took place on June 3 during a dance. During the performance, a young man allegedly touched Dimple's waist. In protest, she slapped him on stage. Dimple later shared a video of the incident, bringing the matter into the public spotlight. stories.title: Johnny-Jojo who made Premanand Maharaj laugh go missing:Comedian Rahul allegedly forgot them in e-rickshaw; Vrindavan police launch search
stories.summary: The teddy bear cartoons Johnny-Jojo that made Premanand Maharaj laugh have gone missing. Johnny and Jojo are puppets of Rahul, a famous comedian artist from Jaipur. Rahul Mishra had come to Vrindavan with his friend to do the parikrama. When he returned after completing the parikrama, he forgot his bag in the e-rickshaw. As soon as Rahul remembered his bag, he stopped the e-rickshaw driver, but instead of stopping, he ran away. Rahul has filed a complaint with the police about Johnny-Jojo going missing. Now Vrindavan police are engaged in searching for the e-rickshaw driver and Jojo. Comedian Rahul had come to Vrindavan for Parikrama Rahul Mishra had come to Vrindavan on Thursday with his friend to do the Parikrama. After completing the Parikrama that night, Rahul took an e-rickshaw from near Chamunda Temple. He was heading to Hotel Sukhdham located on Keshav Dham Road. Meanwhile, he remembered his bag, in which his cartoon characters Johnny Jojo were kept. It was around 1 AM at night. Rahul chased the e-rickshaw to get his bag, but instead of stopping, the e-rickshaw driver fled. Rahul became sad over Jojo's disappearance. He reached Vrindavan Kotwali on Friday and filed a complaint with the police. The police are searching for the e-rickshaw driver through CCTV cameras installed around the hotel. Rahul's emotional connection with Johnny-Jojo Saddened by the disappearance of Johnny-Jojo, Rahul said - I have an emotional connection with both of them. He has entertained Premanand Maharaj through Johnny-Jojo. Rahul said that somehow I should get my Johnny and Jojo back soon. The comedian has also made an emotional appeal on social media searching for Johnny-Jojo. He said that both of them are my life, whoever has taken them, please return them. Station House Officer Sanjay Pandey informed that a case has been registered in the matter and a search is being conducted for Johnny and Jojo. Had met Premanand Ji a year ago A year ago, during a meeting with Premanand Ji Maharaj in Vrindavan, Jojo and Johnny had conversed with him. At which he kept laughing continuously and said- 'How do these toys speak by themselves? This is a wonderful art.' He had also appreciated this art a lot. Rahul had said - Premanandji gave 500-500 as rewards to my Jojo and Johnny. He honored me and made me accept prasad. Young people like us are his devotees and follow his words and discourses. As soon as I came out, the Brijwasis surrounded me. Everyone started saying that we have never seen Maharajji laughing so much, you have done wonders. Rahul started his career with theater, but due to insufficient earnings in this field, he created a YouTube channel in 2015. His friends made him a puppet, with which he created videos. His videos went viral on TikTok, but real success came when he further refined his art and reached bigger platforms. Rahul has been part of many big shows. He reached the Bigg Boss set for a special performance. He has also showcased his art on India's Got Talent.

stories.title: Weather turns across 43 districts in UP:Heavy rain alert in Mau, Ghazipur; storm alert in 21 districts
stories.summary: The spell of thunderstorms and rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Weather conditions changed suddenly on Saturday afternoon. After bright sunshine since morning, Mau and Ghazipur received heavy rainfall around 2 pm. Strong winds blowing at speeds of nearly 50 kmph accompanied thunderclouds. Gorakhpur also witnessed a dust storm. The change in weather brought relief from the intense heat that had prevailed since morning. Late on Friday night, Varanasi also received heavy rain accompanied by lightning. The weather turned pleasant after nearly half an hour of torrential rainfall. Kaushambi witnessed light drizzle in the morning. In Amethi, a mother and daughter died after a mud wall collapsed, while a boy sustained serious injuries. Earlier in the day, districts including Lucknow and Kanpur witnessed bright sunshine. However, humidity in the air kept temperatures slightly lower than usual. The Meteorological Department has issued a light rain alert for 43 districts across the state, while 21 districts are likely to witness thunderstorms and strong winds. Weather experts said the impact of the western disturbance will end within the next 24 hours. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Meteorologist at the Regional Meteorological Center in Lucknow, said- Even today, there is a possibility of storms, strong winds, and scattered drizzles in UP. From tomorrow, all rain systems will cease. Then, there will be intense heat until the monsoon rains. Heatwave conditions will also develop. Considering the current circumstances, the monsoon is likely to enter the state via Gorakhpur by June 24. With that, the spell of rain and thunderstorms that has continued for the past 12 days is expected to come to an end. Temperatures are then likely to rise sharply, with mercury expected to jump by 5°C to 6°C and cross 45°C. A fresh spell of heatwave conditions is also likely to begin from June 9. During the previous 24 hours, strong winds and intermittent rain were recorded in districts including Lucknow, Mau, Bijnor and Agra. In most other districts, strong sunshine pushed temperatures higher. Varanasi was the hottest city in the state with a maximum temperature of 42.2°C, while Hardoi recorded the lowest night temperature at 22°C. Based on current weather patterns, the monsoon is expected to enter Uttar Pradesh through the Gorakhpur region by around June 24. Heavy rain lashed Varanasi late on Friday night, accompanied by thunder and lightning.

stories.title: Jesus’s ‘holy blood’ served in UP’s secret church:Pastor questions idol worship; reporter’s conversion caught on camera
stories.summary: "You people have done a lot of idol worship before coming here, what benefit did you get? You don't have to do all this now. If you go to a temple, don't eat prasad. This is the holy blood of Jesus (red colored juice), it will bring healing (end illness) to the body, you will get rid of difficulties." A pastor who had arrived from Nepal allegedly converted a Dainik Bhaskar reporter—who was posing as a labourer in front of him—to Christianity. According to inputs, such conversion meetings are held every Sunday in a “secret church” in a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri district. It is alleged that to avoid police scrutiny, only the religion is changed while names and caste identities remain unchanged. In the ongoing investigation, it has been reported that when the Bhaskar reporter reached the village in disguise, he was called inside and gradually influenced. The sacred thread (kalava) was allegedly removed, and instructions were given to stop worshipping traditional deities. The full investigation now reveals a pattern of alleged inducement, conversion attempts, surveillance, and systematic religious change. We were called to Pastor Vijay's house in Dalrajpur village of Lakhimpur Kheri district. Here again, 3 people surrounded the reporter and started tempting him... Shivprasad's wife: If you accept this (religion), you will get healed (disease will end) very quickly. Pastor Vijay: (Elaborating on the woman's statement) This is their face today. Tell us after 10-15 days. Shivprasad's wife: Oh, what 15 days, it will happen right now. Just accept it. We will pray. In their name. We did it immediately. We said - brother, free us from this. We have become very troubled. Reporter: We also want to accept it. Shivprasad's wife: (laughing) We understand your pain, brother, but it takes time. Baba has left Nepal. After agreeing to convert to Christianity, we left from there. He asked us to call at 1 PM. When we called, Pastor Vijay said - You come over, Guruji has arrived from Nepal. We reached the spot within half an hour. After that, the game of religious conversion began. Pastor Vijay: We will get you converted very soon, you will have to dedicate your life, you will have to give your life to the Lord quickly. Reporter: Whatever you say, we will do. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: If you want to convert, you can do it now. Reporter: If we convert, will the routine of life change somewhat? Will we have to do something? Nepali Pastor Jeevan: What is that right now you are a slave to sin, whatever it wants you to do, you do. When you accept Jesus, you come out of that sin. (After this, Pastor Vijay showed us Bible verses on his mobile) Pastor Vijay: So are you ready to give your life to the Lord? Reporter: Yes. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: This is not religious conversion, this is our life transformation. Today you have a life of addiction, tomorrow if you are cured, that is not religion, that is life transformation. We want to change your life. Pastor Vijay: Our caste hasn't changed. Language hasn't changed. Whatever is written on our Aadhaar card, it should remain the same. Reporter: Like the kalawa (sacred thread) was cut, there are many such worship items kept at home. Then what will be done about them? Pastor Vijay: We will reach your home. Gradually, that will be removed from your mind. After this, beginning the acceptance process, Pastor Vijay started the prayer and asked the reporter to repeat. Pastor Vijay: Lord, I am a sinful man. I confess all my sins and unrighteousness. Lord, you left heaven for me and came to this world. You took my sins upon yourself and gave your life. And I believe. God raised you to life on the third day. From today I accept you into my life calling you my Savior Lord. From today I accept you calling you my Master, calling you Savior. From today I surrender my life into your hands. From today may you take control of my life. Lord Jesus, these are your living names. Amen. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Now that you have accepted Jesus, you have become a child of Jesus. Now to leave the bad habits, Pastor ji will fellowship with you. As you come into fellowship, the bad habits will be left behind. Reporter: Like we did the acceptance prayer, now what changes will come in our life? Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Now after going home, you will not do worship and all that. Pastor Vijay: Look, you are new, after waking up in the morning you can make a phone call. When waking up, at sleeping time we will do prayer. Reporter: The worship and incense sticks etc. that we light in the morning, should we do that or not? Pastor Vijay: (Shaking his head in refusal) Don't worship. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: It makes a difference from idol worship, because we don't do idol worship. Before you people came here, you had done a lot of idol worship, right? So what benefit did you get? You don't have to do all that. Whatever Pastor ji says, you have to do accordingly. Reporter: Do we need to tell anyone right now or not, in the family, among friends? Pastor Vijay: Don't tell anyone right now. Tell the family, but later. Nepali Pastor Jeevan: Right now you just say this - Jesus, heal me. After this, Nepali Pastor Jeevan offered a final prayer for the reporter. After the conversion, the reporter was advised to call Pastor Vijay morning and evening. We called Vijay twice daily for a week. He repeatedly asked to come home. Along with that, he kept reminding that you belong to Jesus and also tempted with the promise of ending the illness soon. Reporter: Guruji, I want to ask one thing - we are going home and my wife is very religious. She will want to do puja-paath (worship rituals), so should I stop her or what should I do? Pastor Vijay: Well, you haven't learned much from us yet, but when the whole family comes in line, it will be good. Just as you accepted Jesus that day. You became His son, became His servant, similarly we will make your wife accept too. The Lord has said that if one person trusts in Me, I will save his entire household. The Lord will definitely help, will change her (wife's) mind. She will also believe. Reporter: So right now we don't need to do anything, right? If my wife does puja-paath, we should let her do it, right? Pastor Vijay: Yes, let her do it for now. When complete peace comes to your mind, then we will all together explain to her. Reporter: We can't even light incense sticks, right? Pastor Vijay: Can't light them. In the conversation, Pastor Vijay mentioned that their network is connected to Nepal. Pastor Vijay: They (senior religious leaders) live towards Kathmandu. Your matter has been conveyed to them. They are also now praying for you. Reporter: I see, can I meet them? Pastor Vijay: Meeting them happens only with great fortune. We succeeded at every step of the conversion gang. When they were fully convinced, they called us for complete conversion after a week. This time we wanted to expose the entire racket of the gang. Therefore, we included two fellow reporters. We told Pastor Vijay that there are two people we know. One is a Sikh and the other is a Muslim. Both of them are also trapped in troubles, will their problems also end like ours? The pastor immediately asked to bring them to the secret church on Sunday. We reached the healing assembly at 8 AM on Sunday morning. There were 50 men and women in the hall. Pastor Vijay was in front of them. A cross was placed on the table. Vijay was delivering Jesus's teachings. We sat on the chairs arranged there. Where the game of complete conversion of the first reporter and starting the conversion process of the two reporters who accompanied him took place. Pastor Vijay: Today in the arrangement that has been made, you will be included (complete conversion). Reporter: Okay. Shivprasad Gautam: Those who are new people, they will not be included. Only you will be included in this arrangement. After this, prayers were held and people present there were given red-colored juice to drink one by one. This was called the sacred blood of Jesus. Reporter: What is this sherbet? Shivprasad Gautam: No, this is sacred blood. This will bring healing to your body. You will get relief from troubles. The pastor made the reporter stand and introduced him to everyone and then prayed for the reporter. This meant that the reporter's complete conversion had now taken place. Reporter: How can we reach the Guruji from Kathmandu? Pastor Vijay: Now they will only come if called. If everyone says so, we will call them. They will come. They are 60 years old now, but even today their face has more glow than yours. Reporter: What is their name? Pastor Vijay: The name is Ravi Sharma. stories.title: Meerut CMO under probe for favouring ex-MLA:Allegedly helped him gain crores; NHM scam charge resurfaces
stories.summary: Dr. Ashok Kataria, who was the CMO of Meerut, has been accused of corruption. Following this, he has been attached to the Health Directorate in Lucknow. The allegation is that Dr. Kataria illegally benefited the companies of former Congress MLA Mukesh Srivastava, who was involved in the National Health Mission (NHM) scam, to the tune of crores of rupees. Maintenance contracts for hospitals in Meerut and Shravasti were given to the firm of the former MLA's brother, and then bills were passed without verification. An investigation into these irregularities in the CMO office is being conducted at the Additional Director (AD) level. CMO handed over GeM portal ID to former MLA In 2024, a private firm was given a contract to administer Hepatitis-B vaccines in Muzaffarnagar. The firm was charging people 60 rupees for the vaccine, whereas it should have been free. When the matter came to light, the contract was cancelled, but no action was taken against the responsible Additional Chief Medical Officer Mahesh Chandra. It is alleged that Dr. Ashok Kataria handed over the department's GeM portal (an online public procurement portal of the Government of India) ID to Mukesh Srivastava. Mukesh used it from his private office in Lucknow. In January 2025, when an investigation was conducted at the government level, purchase orders worth approximately 3 crore rupees were cancelled. Later, orders were reissued based on old notesheets. In February, BJP leader from Meerut, Ankit Chaudhary, complained about this to CM Yogi. Former MLA is the main accused in NHM scam Mukesh Srivastava (now SP leader), who was a Congress MLA from Payagpur in Bahraich, is the main accused in the NHM scam that took place in Shravasti. He is accused of embezzling crores in the purchase of medicines, medical equipment and vehicles in hospitals in the district between 2017-22. The vigilance team registered a case on May 30 this year. Along with Mukesh, an FIR has been registered against 6 people including two former CMOs of Shravasti, Dr. Dinesh Kumar Singh and Dr. Vipendra Kumar Singh. Fake bills passed after taking 25% bribe In Shravasti, from 2017 to 22, vouchers were passed without creating a medical reimbursement register. Payments were made after taking 10 to 25% commission. The hospital maintenance work was given to Mukesh's brother's company RP Construction. The company got bills passed by showing work on paper. In the case, an FIR has also been filed against Rajendra Prasad Srivastava, proprietor of RP Group of Construction. A case of disproportionate assets has also been registered against Mukesh Srivastava. The vigilance investigation found that during 2017 to 2022, Mukesh earned approximately Rs 1.12 crore from all legitimate sources, while he spent approximately Rs 1.80 crore. Investigation into the difference between income and expenditure is ongoing.

stories.title: Friend killed coaching operator for gold worth around ₹10 lakh:Watched Crime Patrol, searched YouTube; wore burqa to hide identity
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the murder of coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta was allegedly carried out by his 18-year-old friend, Mohit Dwivedi. Police said the motive was robbery, not personal enmity. Mohit allegedly targeted gold bracelets and chains worth around ₹10 lakh. According to Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal, Mohit had been planning the crime for nearly 15 days. During this period, he searched YouTube for ways to kill a friend without revealing his identity and watched several episodes of Crime Patrol to learn how to evade police investigation. To avoid being identified, Mohit allegedly disguised himself in a burqa, ladies' slippers, a purse, a dupatta and gloves. On the night of May 31, he reached the coaching centre in an auto-rickshaw and attempted the robbery. Police said that when Vijay resisted, Mohit pushed him forcefully, causing him to fall and suffer a severe head injury. Vijay lost consciousness and later died. After the incident, Mohit allegedly dragged the body into another room before fleeing. The murder came to light on the morning of June 1, when a female teacher arrived at the coaching centre and found Vijay's blood-soaked body. She immediately alerted the police, who launched an investigation. See 2 pictures- Both went to visit Khajuraho together on Holi Commissioner Raghubir Lal informed- Coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta, a resident of Azad Nagar in Nawabganj, and accused Mohit Dwivedi had known each other for the past 18 years. Both ran coaching centers in the same building. They often spent time together. They used to drink alcohol together and also gambled. Mohit's wife had left him several years ago. Some time after this, his coaching center also shut down. Then he started working in labor supply for a company. During Holi, Mohit and Vijay had gone to Khajuraho together for sightseeing. It was there that Mohit's eyes fell on Vijay's gold bracelet and chain worth around 10 lakh rupees. From that very moment, he had started planning to loot these jewels. Bought burqa, ladies' slippers, purse, dupatta, gloves from the market Accused Mohit Dwivedi had planned the robbery around May 15. He watched several episodes of Crime Patrol. He also searched on YouTube how to commit murder by hiding one's identity. About a week before the murder, he went to the weekly Monday market in Nawabganj. From there he bought a burqa, ladies' slippers, purse, dupatta and gloves. He reached near the coaching center wearing a burqa. He also did reconnaissance of all the routes to escape after the robbery. He also checked which routes and places had CCTV cameras installed. Pretended to be mute, reached station to show Kannauj connection After completing the recce, on May 31 at around 3:30 PM in the afternoon, Mohit reached JK Cancer Hospital located in Swaroop Nagar in his car. After parking the car there, he went inside the hospital and came out wearing a burqa after some time. After this, he reached Anwarganj Railway Station by auto. At around 5:30 PM in the evening, he started waiting for the train coming from Kannauj, so that the police would think that the person who committed the crime had come from Kannauj. After the train arrived, Mohit came out of the station and sat in an auto. To prove himself mute, he gave the auto driver Vijay's coaching address written on a slip of paper. The auto driver took him to the coaching center with the help of Google Maps. Reached coaching on pretext of admission, snatched chain-bracelet by pushing Around 6:45 PM in the evening, Mohit got down from the auto about 20 meters before the coaching center. After waiting for about 10 minutes, he reached Vijay Prakash Gupta. He gave a slip and wrote about taking admission in the coaching. On this, Vijay asked him to wait for 10 minutes, saying he was going to take a bath. When Vijay returned after some time, Mohit tried to snatch his gold chain. When he resisted, there was a scuffle between the two. During this, Mohit gave Vijay a strong push, due to which he fell and became unconscious. After this, Mohit looted his gold chain and bracelet. The accused dragged Vijay to another room of the coaching center. Then he fled from the spot. After murder, reached Nawabganj from Swaroop Nagar Inspector Shiv Kumar posted in the cyber cell said - After the murder, the police started examining the footage of CCTV cameras installed nearby. During the investigation, a suspect wearing a burqa was seen at several places. The police examined about 500 CCTV footages. The footage revealed that after the incident, the person wearing the burqa reached Nawabganj through the lanes of Swaroop Nagar. From the guava market near Ganga Barrage, he took an auto and went towards the road leading to Gurudev. After getting down from the auto in Gurudev, he walked towards Rawatpur Station. From there, he took an auto and reached JK Cancer Hospital. After some time, a young man came out of the hospital and sat in a car, heading towards Nawabganj via Motijheel. The young man's face was clearly visible in the CCTV footage. Based on this, the police identified him. After that, Mohit Dwivedi, a resident of Azad Nagar, was taken into custody and interrogated. During interrogation, he broke down and confessed to the murder and robbery. Vijay Prakash's body was found in the coaching centre On Monday morning, the body of coaching operator Vijay Prakash Gupta was found at Data Expert Computer Coaching Institute located in Azad Nagar, Nawabganj. A female teacher who arrived at the coaching center in the morning saw his body lying in the room, after which she raised an alarm. She informed the people nearby. As soon as the information was received, police and forensic team reached the spot and started investigation. The deceased's brother Vikas Gupta had told the police that Vijay's gold chain and bracelet were missing, while 15 thousand rupees were found in his pocket. Based on this, the police had suspected murder after robbery. Accused has completed MA-LLB DCP Central, ADCP, Nawabganj Police and the Surveillance Team were able to reach the accused based on forensic evidence, CCTV footage and technical investigation. During interrogation, Mohit Dwivedi confessed to the entire conspiracy of murder and robbery. Police have recovered the stolen gold chain, bracelet and other crucial evidence from the possession of the accused. After this, he was arrested and sent to jail. The accused Mohit Dwivedi is educated. He has completed BA, LLB and MA. He had also recently appeared for the TGT examination.

stories.title: Pastor who fed 'Jesus' blood' for conversion arrested:Associate govt teacher also arrested; UP police raids secret church
stories.summary: After revelations of alleged religious conversions along the UP-Nepal border, police launched action and arrested Pastor Vijay and his associate, government teacher Shivprasad Gautam, on Monday. Both were produced in court and sent to jail. In Dalrajpur village of Lakhimpur Kheri district, Hindus were allegedly being converted to Christianity on a large scale. To investigate, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter posed as a laborer and spent 20 days in the village. Members of the group later approached him and allegedly offered inducements to convert. Using a hidden camera, the reporter exposed the alleged conversion network and those involved. After the report was published, Kheri police raided the secret church on June 6, but the pastor and his associates escaped. They were arrested on June 8 and later sent to jail by the court. Case registered under sections of religious conversion After Bhaskar's investigation, people who converted from Hinduism to Christianity came forward openly. This gang had also lured Mohit Chaudhary of the Tharu community. On Mohit's complaint, a case was registered against Pastor Vijay and teacher Shivprasad Gautam under 4 sections. Mohit said that Vijay took him to Dalrajpur, where he pressured him to adopt Christianity. He said, 'If you adopt Christianity, you will get money.' Master Shivkumar also arrived there. Then both of them pressured me to adopt Christianity and also offered temptations. When I refused, they started threatening to kill me.

stories.title: Minister Nandi stripped of expressway portfolio:UPEIDA to report directly to CM Yogi amid IAS row
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' suffered a major setback on Monday as the state government withdrew his charge of the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA). The government has shifted UPEIDA from the Industrial Development Department to the Infrastructure and Industrial Development Department, bringing all expressway construction and development work directly under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Until now, project, budget, and approval files related to UPEIDA were routed through Nandi's department. Under the new arrangement, they will be cleared directly by the Chief Minister's Office. Why did the government make the change? The government said the move will improve coordination between infrastructure and industrial development departments, speed up decision-making, and reduce project delays. However, political circles view it as a setback for Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' following the controversy during the transfer season. The decision is also being linked to his ongoing tussle with Additional Chief Secretary Alok Kumar. Sources said Nandi had raised objections over officer appointments and deputations in UPEIDA and frequently intervened in its functioning. He had also recently complained to CM Yogi about Alok Kumar. To keep UPEIDA's operations free from such interference, it has now been shifted to the Infrastructure Department, which is directly overseen by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Nandi also opened a front against the former Chief Secretary Last year, Nand Gopal Nandi had also opened a front against the then Chief Secretary Manoj Kumar Singh. He had advocated against giving him a service extension by complaining all the way to Delhi. The Government of India did not grant a service extension to Manoj Kumar Singh. However, CM Yogi had appointed him as the Vice Chairman of the Transformation Commission. UPEIDA formed in 2007 UPIDA was constituted on December 27, 2007, for the construction of expressways and the development of industrial corridors in the state. In later years, its role primarily focused on the construction of expressways and large infrastructure projects. Infrastructure is UPIDA's primary function Government officials say that UPIDA's core work is to develop infrastructure. Industries are promoted only after expressways, roads, and other large projects are completed. For this reason, it has been decided to bring it under the Infrastructure Development Department. Project monitoring to improve The order from the Secretariat Administration Department states that the new system will improve the monitoring, implementation, and coordination of projects between departments. Additionally, decisions related to expressways and other major projects will be made more quickly than before. Nandi stripped of the charge of Banda's Guardian Minister 5 days earlier The Yogi government had made a major reshuffle in the districts of guardian ministers about 5 days ago. During this, the guardian minister of Banda district was also changed. Dinesh Pratap Singh was made the guardian minister of Banda district. Before this, Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi' was the guardian minister of Banda district, who was removed. Now know about Minister Nandi Nand Gopal Gupta 'Nandi', a BJP MLA from Prayagraj South, was born on April 23, 1974, into a middle-class family in Prayagraj and is also a successful businessman. He first won the Allahabad South assembly seat on a BSP ticket in 2007 and became a minister in the Mayawati government. He later contested the 2014 Lok Sabha election on a Congress ticket but lost. Nandi joined the BJP in 2017, won the assembly election, and retained the seat in 2022 before joining the Yogi Adityanath cabinet. His wife, Abhilasha Gupta, has served as Mayor of Prayagraj. On July 12, 2010, Nandi survived a deadly remote-controlled bomb attack in Prayagraj in which he was seriously injured. Since then, he has celebrated July 12 every year as his 'rebirth' or 'recovered birthday.'

stories.title: ‘I can’t marry you, but I’ll keep meeting you’:Ayodhya preacher accused of rape goes missing after FIR; audio clip surfaces
stories.summary: After a rape case was registered against Ayodhya preacher Pawan Dev Maharaj (42), police launched a search for him. His residence was raided several times on Sunday night, but he was not found. Efforts to arrest him are ongoing. On Monday, Bikapur police also conducted the victim's medical examination. Meanwhile, a 6-minute-30-second audio clip of a conversation between Pawan Dev Maharaj and the woman from Bihar who filed the complaint has surfaced. Recorded two days before the FIR was lodged on June 4, the audio allegedly captures the preacher speaking emotionally with the woman. 2 pictures of the preacher In the audio that has surfaced, Pawan Dev Maharaj talks about giving land and property to the woman. Whereas, the woman repeatedly asks only for his name and the right of a wife. The woman told Bhaskar that this audio is of her conversation with the storyteller. Read the conversation between the preacher and the woman Preacher: What should I do? Where should I go? It's not my fault. I will give you all my property. Woman: I don't want anything, I just want your name. Preacher: How can I give you my name? My family won't agree. I have married you, applied vermilion to you, asked for you from God, but nothing more can happen now. Woman: I don't want anything. If you are not there, what will I do with the property? Preacher: So tell me, what should I do? Should I leave the world? Woman: No, I just don't want anything. In the leaked audio, Pawan Dev Maharaj allegedly asks the woman if she can live separately while he continues to support her, visit her, and stay in touch. He even suggests changing her appearance through plastic surgery so no one can recognise her. The woman rejects the proposal, saying she does not want land, a house, or a separate residence. She insists on living with him as his wife. Maharaj is then heard asking how he could bring her home as his bride, while the woman repeatedly says she only wants to live in his house as his wife, not alone. Complete case in 10 points Police registered a case Based on the woman's complaint, Bikapur Kotwali police registered a case on Saturday night (June 6). The matter is from the Bikapur area, about 25 kilometres away from the district headquarters. Police are investigating the allegations and raiding possible hideouts in search of the preacher. Police officers say that further action will be taken based on the investigation of the case. On Monday, Bikapur police conducted a medical examination of the victim woman. Meanwhile, since the registration of the case, silence has fallen over the storyteller's house. His family members are also avoiding coming forward. Know about Pawan Dev Pawan Dev Maharaj hails from Malethu Kanak village in the Bikapur police station area. He describes himself as a disciple of the famous preacher Devkinandan Thakur. In the last few years, he has made a name for himself in the religious world through his narratives. Pawan Dev Maharaj was appointed as the national spokesperson of Karni Sena on May 13, 2026. Since then, he also speaks on various social and religious issues related to the organisation. Along with religious platforms, he is also recognised as a young preacher and speaker. Pawan Dev's father, Ramakant Shastri, is a ritualist. He remains associated with him in religious rituals and worship at the family level. Police officers say that all aspects are being investigated based on the complaint. Further action will be taken based on the available evidence and statements from both parties. stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Claim of ₹7 cr theft from Ram Mandir sparks row; INDIA Bloc reaches 5-point consensus in New Delhi meeting more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. INDIA bloc reaches 5-point consensus, will write letter to CJI The 7th meeting of the INDIA bloc concludes in Delhi. During a press briefing, Congress National President Mallikarjun Kharge claimed that a 5-point consensus has been reached among the stakeholders. 2. ₹7 cr Ram Temple theft claim triggers row; Shankaracharya says, ‘What else when a thief is made guardian?’ A political controversy has erupted over allegations that crores of rupees were stolen from Ram Temple donations in Ayodhya. Speaking in Agra, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said, 'When a thief is made the protector, what else can be expected?' He alleged that after controversies over land deals, money is now being taken directly from the donation box. 3. UP police aspirant in tears after exam, calls maths section tough; 2.8 lakh competing for 32,679 posts The UP Police recruitment exam for 32,679 constable posts is being held across the state. Candidates underwent strict checks, including admit card verification, biometric matching, and retina scans. In some centres, women were asked to open hair buns, while chains and spectacles were removed for inspection. 4. 32 dead, over 200 injured in Philippines earthquake A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the Philippines on Monday morning, causing damage to several buildings. Most of the affected structures include shops, offices, and commercial buildings. AP reported, citing officials, that the death toll from the quake has risen to 32. 5. 4 UP MPs fall ill during Ladakh tour; one admitted to AIIMS Four MPs from Uttar Pradesh fell ill during a visit to Leh-Ladakh due to high-altitude oxygen shortages. Lalganj MP was admitted to AIIMS after vomiting blood, while other MPs required oxygen support because of breathing difficulties. 6. Businessman’s murder accused killed in STF encounter; had 41 cases against him Bhanu Pratap Singh alias Bablu (38), a ₹2 lakh reward-carrying criminal wanted in a businessman’s murder case, was killed in an encounter with the UP STF in Ayodhya on Sunday night. Police said he was intercepted while fleeing on a motorcycle with an accomplice. 7. Iran says stopping strikes on Israel, will resume if Israel attacks Lebanon Iran's central military headquarters has announced it will halt strikes on Israel, but warned that it would launch a "more severe" response if Israel continues its attacks in southern Lebanon. The statement came after US President Donald Trump urged both countries to stop "shooting", following their first direct exchanges of attacks since the ceasefire agreed in April. 8. Haryanvi dancer seeks justice after on-stage molestation in Hathras A Haryanvi dancer has demanded strict action against a youth accused of molesting her during a stage performance in Hathras. Police have registered an FIR against an unidentified accused under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). She said she wants such “beasts” punished. 9. ‘Gym trainer trapped my son, got him converted’; Shamli businessman alleges property grab plot A Shamli medicine businessman has alleged that gym trainer Chandni Qureshi trapped his 27-year-old son, converted him from Hinduism to Islam, and arranged a fake nikah to gain access to family property worth crores. He also claimed his son spent hours watching content from a Pakistani YouTube channel. 10. Parliamentary panel asks NTA to define ‘paper leak’ A parliamentary committee probing controversies related to the NEET paper leak and CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system has raised several pointed questions to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and CBSE.

stories.title: ‘I became Muslim of my own free will’:Shamli trader’s son defends conversion; stands by gym-trainer wife
stories.summary: Ayush Malik, who converted to Islam after marrying a Muslim female gym trainer in Shamli, UP, appeared before the media on Monday. He said, No one pressured me to convert to Islam. I accepted Islam of my own free will. My parents perform puja, and I offer namaz five times a day. I have also kept a beard because it is a Sunnah in our Islam. Ayush claimed he had been studying Islam and Muslim customs for about 13 years and had married gym trainer Chandni Qureshi under Islamic rites four years ago. He said he kept the marriage secret because his sister was unmarried at the time. ‘I am now a Muslim. Both families are mine, and I will not abandon either of them,’ he said. Ayush's father, Devraj Malik, is a wealthy medicine businessman in Shamli with assets worth crores. On Saturday, he filed an FIR against Chandni, six of her family members, and three Maulvis, alleging forced conversion and illegal extortion. Police have arrested Chandni and her father and sent them to jail. Full statement of Ayush Malik alias Rehman Ayush Malik, alias Rehman, said he embraced Islam on his own and was not influenced by anyone. He said his interest in Islam began during his school years and deepened around 2012-13. He regularly watched videos of Pakistani Islamic preacher DrDr Israr Ahmed, which further strengthened his inclination. Ayush said he rarely visited temples as a child because he felt drawn toward Islam. He now offers namaz five times a day and keeps a beard, which he described as a Sunnah followed by Islamic prophets. He said he later met Chandni and, four years ago, wholeheartedly accepted Islam before marrying her according to Islamic rituals. According to Ayush, neither Chandni nor her family pressured him to convert, and the decision was entirely his own. He added that his family is upset because he left Hinduism and adopted Islam, but maintained it was a personal choice. He said he had planned to inform them gradually, but they learned about it earlier. In February, he publicly announced that he had accepted Islam. Ayush said, Lying is a sin in Islam, but Islam allows a truth to be concealed if the situation is not right, if life is at stake, or if someone's feelings are being hurt. Another reason was that my sister was not married yet. Chandni's family was also insistent on getting their daughter married quickly, so I converted to Islam and married Chandni, keeping it a secret from my family.Even if my family doesn't accept me, for me, both my family and Chandni's family are my own. I cannot leave anyone. I will stand by the full truth regarding the accusations my family has made against Chandni and her father. My mother still calls me by my childhood name, Lavkush, and I don't object. She is my mother, she can call me whatever she wants.Currently, I am a Muslim, and I am happy. I will never change my religion again, no matter how much pressure anyone puts on me. Islam also does not permit this. 2 pictures How the dispute started The case involves Dayanand Nagar and Qureshi Basti in Shamli. Devraj Malik, a medicine businessman, president of the Shamli Chemist Association, and resident of Dayanand Nagar, alleged that his son Ayush was influenced by Chandni, a gym trainer from Qureshi Basti. According to police, Ayush, who runs a medical store after completing B-Pharma, started visiting the 'Qureshi Plus' gym five years ago, where he met Chandni. Devraj claims Chandni drew Ayush into a relationship and secretly married him under Islamic rites four years ago. He further alleged that Ayush began changing his appearance about six months ago, first growing a beard and later regularly visiting a mosque. Photos have surfaced showing Ayush offering Namaz in a mosque and wearing a cap and kurta-pyjama at his medical store. Mahant released a video, then the matter came to light The matter came to light when, on June 4, Mahant Swami Yashveer of Yog Sadhana Ashram in Muzaffarnagar released a video. He stated that Chandni Qureshi has trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. Under pressure, the entire family has converted to their religion. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations started protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in at the gym trainer's house. On Saturday, Ayush's father, Devraj Malik, reached the police station and filed an FIR. SP NP Singh stated that a case has been registered and an investigation has begun. This is 'property jihad' to usurp property worth 60-70 crores Religious leader Yashveer Maharaj said, This case is not just 'love jihad', but also 'property jihad' to usurp property worth 60-70 crores. He claimed that the accused Chandni Qureshi has extorted about one and a half crore rupees from the youth. The threads of this conspiracy are suspected to be linked to religious leaders in Delhi, Mumbai and Pakistan. Father said - I am a Hindu, my son was converted to Muslim Businessman Devraj Malik told Dainik Bhaskar that his son Ayush's conversion was carried out by gym trainer Chandni Qureshi and her family members. They had been extorting money from his son for 5 years. He stated that all this happened under a conspiracy. It also involves Munawwar Maulvi, a resident near Kadian Mosque in Azad Chowk, and 2 other unknown Maulvis. All of them together put mental pressure on his son. They forced him to adopt the Muslim religion. When we found out, we protested against it. My wife and I are still in the Hindu religion. We go to the temple for worship in the morning and evening.

stories.title: Suspended cop behind ₹2 cr Hapur robbery:Businessman’s family held at gunpoint; police arrest all five accused
stories.summary: The mastermind behind the ₹2 crore robbery at a businessman's house in Hapur was a suspended Uttar Pradesh Police constable, Vicky Gautam. Police arrested Gautam and his four accomplices late Sunday night following an encounter. During the encounter, two accused suffered bullet injuries to their legs. Police said the gang had surveyed timber businessman Narendra Agarwal's residence for four months before carrying out the robbery on June 2. The accused held the family hostage for nearly an hour and fled with 1.25 kg of gold, silver jewellery, and cash. All five suspects were captured on CCTV footage. Gautam had also been arrested about a year ago for possessing old currency worth ₹1.5 crore. Know how the robbery happened On the early morning of June 2, 17-year-old Siddhant, grandson of businessman Narendra Agarwal, returned home from a business tour to find robbers already lying in wait. As he entered, four armed men followed him inside. When Siddhant tried to raise an alarm, the robbers pointed a pistol at his temple and overpowered him. The gang then held Narendra Agarwal, his wife Sushila, and the watchman at gunpoint. They demanded ₹2 crore in cash, but Agarwal told them there was not that much money in the house. The accused then tied up everyone with bedsheets, locked them in a room, and spent about an hour ransacking the house. 1.25 kg of gold and lakhs in cash looted The robbers fled with around 1.25 kg of gold jewellery, silver, and lakhs of rupees in cash taken from cupboards and lockers. After they left, the family alerted the police. Senior officers, including the DIG and SP, reached the spot and began examining CCTV footage. The robbery at the home of a prominent businessman triggered outrage among traders. A trade association questioned the law-and-order situation and gave police a 72-hour ultimatum to solve the case, warning of market closures and protests. During the investigation, police found CCTV footage about 150 metres from Narendra Agarwal's house, showing three youths fleeing on a single motorcycle with a bag after the crime. The footage helped identify the accused. How police tracked down the robbers CO Varun Mishra said, Late Sunday night, police were checking on Sultanpur Road in the Kotwali Dehat area. During this, five suspicious youths on two bikes were seen approaching. When the police tried to stop them, the criminals increased the speed of their bikes and started firing at the police team.In retaliation, Rohit and Shahbe Alam, residents of Moradabad, were injured by police firing. Police cordoned off the area and apprehended suspended constable Vicky Gautam along with his three other accused. All five accused are in police custody. Both injured have been admitted to the hospital for treatment. Kept doing reconnaissance for four months Police investigation revealed that the gang had extensively reconnoitred the businessman's house before committing the crime. Initial investigation revealed two months of reconnaissance, while later investigation showed that the criminals had been monitoring the activities of the house and family for about four months. Information was gathered on visitors, security arrangements, people present in the house, and even the safe's location. Mason's son revealed the locker's location In the robbery case, police have also arrested Guddu, a resident of Rustampur Sarai (Moradabad), and Tinkoo, a resident of Sambhal Road. Tinkoo's father, Satpal, is a mason and had been working for the businessman for several months. According to the police, it was Tinkoo who provided the robbers with information about the location of the locker and its key in Narendra Agarwal's house. This is why the accused directly reached the places where cash and valuables were kept. Constable suspended for being absent from duty

stories.title: Claim of ₹7 cr theft from Ram Temple sparks row:Shankaracharya says, ‘This is what happens when a thief is made Guardian’
stories.summary: A political controversy has erupted over allegations that crores of rupees have been stolen from donation collections at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Speaking in Agra, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand criticised the alleged incident, saying, “When a thief is made the protector, what else can be expected? Earlier, it happened in the name of land deals, and now money is allegedly being taken directly from the donation box.” Responding to Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks, Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary said, “Who is making these claims? Akhilesh keeps making statements, and we cannot keep responding to all of them. This is not a government matter; the temple administration will answer it.” Saint Varun Das Maharaj also attacked the SP chief, saying, “Akhilesh Yadav, who troubles devotees of Lord Ram, has no right to speak on this issue.” The controversy began after former SP minister Pawan Pandey alleged on Sunday that around ₹5 crore to ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from the Ram Temple’s donation funds. Akhilesh Yadav subsequently questioned the government's silence on the issue, calling it suspicious and demanding that the court take suo motu cognisance of the matter. In response to the allegations, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust General Secretary Champat Rai issued a clarification. He stated that the trust conducts internal audits regularly, with representatives of both the trust and the State Bank of India participating in the process. According to him, the audit exercise is currently underway, and no evidence of any theft or irregularity has emerged so far. Reacting to Champat Rai’s statement, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Sanjay Singh said the clarification did not categorically deny the alleged theft. “The official statement does not clearly say that no donation money was stolen. That means no clear explanation has been given,” he said. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the saints about theft claims Read the entire matter in detail- Akhilesh wrote - Disappearance of money is shameful for the temple trust Akhilesh posted on X on Sunday and wrote - This is extremely sensitive news for devotees of Lord Ram across the world. Crores of rupees from Ram Temple offerings have been found missing. Akhilesh has also targeted the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust and the government. He wrote that the disappearance of crores of rupees is an extremely shameful situation for the temple trust. No one wants to come forward to give any clarification. The SP president has demanded that the court take suo motu cognisance, as it is directly related to the deep faith of the entire Sanatan society globally in Lord Ram. The government's silence is suspicious. Former Minister's Claim - Rs 7.5 Crore theft occurred Pawan Pandey was the State Minister for Forest and Entertainment Tax in the SP government. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, he claimed that the donation boxes kept inside the Ayodhya Ram Temple, where offerings are made, have been subjected to theft ranging from 5 to 7.50 crores. Names of BJP workers and some people from the Trust are emerging in this. I want to ask the country's government and UP CM Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath whether you will conduct an impartial investigation into this matter? Will an FIR be filed against those thieves? Because the faith of crores of people in the country is connected to that temple. He said that people had offered their hard-earned money, saving rupee by rupee, for the construction of that temple and at the feet of Lord Ram. If such theft happens, it is highly condemnable. The government should immediately take action on this, and whoever is guilty should be sent behind bars. He said that it is not yet clear how long this theft has been going on. Which members of the trust this money has reached should also be investigated. Champat Rai's clarification, Akhilesh's counter-attack - The clarification itself is not clear Message from Champat Rai, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, for everyone's information#vhp #rammandir pic.twitter.com/jEf75NtR — Nishant Rai (निशांत राय) (@Nishantrai13) June 7, 2026 After this, Akhilesh also counterattacked Champat Rai's clarification. Akhilesh wrote on X - The clarification itself is not clear. It seems this is a routine matter for them every week, and so very routine that they don't even consider it 'noteworthy' anymore. The facial expressions and body language are filled with desperation and disappointment. All members of the trust should be seated together and given a clarification, and CCTV evidence should be used to verify the figures. As soon as all the trustees sit together, the truth will immediately come out, because not everyone among them is the same. When no particular person is at the centre of this manipulation suspicion, then what is the importance of any one person's clarification? It should also be clarified why it took so many hours for a 40-second clarification to come, and why even speaking for 1 minute in the name of clarification is proving to be so difficult. Like the state government's silence, this clarification is also suspicious. It seems as if a verbal formality is being fulfilled in the name of clarification. The entire world's Sanatan society has become even more doubtful and hurt by this extremely weak clarification. Know about the system of counting offerings at Ram Mandir... ₹2,475 Crore spent on the Temple In a temple trust meeting on December 13, 2025, it was revealed that the trust has received a total of ₹4,575 crore so far. Over the past 5 years and 9 months, ₹2,475 crore have been spent on temple construction, expansion of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi complex, purchase of land and buildings, and various other works. At that time, the trust had approximately ₹2,100 crore remaining. Ayodhya's Ram Temple receives donations of over ₹1 crore daily Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was formed on February 5, 2020

Meanwhile, Congress MLA from Farenda, Virendra Chaudhary, will also reach the protest site. Loud sloganeering taking place The sloganeering by students sitting on a dharna against the university administration also continued. The students say that action is being taken to raise issues related to student interests. Whereas the university administration itself is adopting a stubborn stance and increasing fees manifold. Announcement to continue movement until demands are met The students sitting on dharna say that their movement will continue until the expulsion is withdrawn and positive decisions are made on other demands, including the fee hike. Meanwhile, no new response has come from the university administration in this matter so far. stories.title: Exam special train to run between Gorakhpur-Lucknow:2 trains to run on Banaras-Azamgarh route
stories.summary: To facilitate candidates appearing for the Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment Examination, the Railway Administration has decided to operate several unreserved special trains on routes under the Gorakhpur Division. In particular, four special trains will run on the Gorakhpur–Lucknow route from June 8 to June 10, providing significant relief to candidates travelling to examination centres. According to railway officials, all coaches in these special trains will be unreserved, and additional coaches may be attached if passenger demand increases. The Railways have also decided to reschedule and regulate some regular train services during this period to ensure smoother operations. Four special trains between Gorakhpur-Lucknow 05005 Gorakhpur-Lucknow Junction Unreserved Examination Special Train will depart daily from Gorakhpur at 1:30 PM from June 8 to 10 and will reach Lucknow Junction at 6:15 PM via Khalilabad, Basti, Babhnan, Mankapur, Gonda, Karnailganj, Barabanki, and Badshahnagar. Meanwhile, the 05006 Lucknow Junction-Gorakhpur Special Train will depart from Lucknow at 1:30 PM during this period and reach Gorakhpur at 6:50 PM. Additionally, for the convenience of night-time passengers, the 05031 Gorakhpur-Lucknow Junction Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 7 PM and reach Lucknow at 12:55 AM the next day. On the return journey, the 05032 Lucknow Junction-Gorakhpur Special Train will depart from Lucknow at 6:15 PM and reach Gorakhpur at 11:55 PM. The Railway has informed that these trains will have a total of 12 coaches, including 10 coaches of General Second Class and Sleeper Class, along with two SLRD coaches. All coaches will be in the unreserved category. Special trains from Varanasi and Azamgarh are also on Gorakhpur route In view of the examination, special arrangements have also been made for candidates reaching Gorakhpur from various districts of Purvanchal. 05149 Varanasi City-Gorakhpur Unreserved Exam Special Train will depart from Varanasi City at 7:30 PM on June 8 and 9 and arrive at Gorakhpur at 2:15 AM. This train will stop at major stations like Mau, Belthra Road, Salempur, Bhatni, Deoria Sadar, and Chauri Chaura. On the return journey, 05150 Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 3:15 AM on June 9 and 10 and reach Varanasi City at 9:15 AM. Similarly, 05139 Azamgarh-Gorakhpur Unreserved Exam Special Train will depart from Azamgarh at 2:30 PM daily from June 8 to 10 and reach Gorakhpur at 7 PM. The 05140 Gorakhpur-Azamgarh Special Train will depart from Gorakhpur at 8 PM and reach Azamgarh at 12:30 AM the next day. Special services for Ballia and Azamgarh as well For the convenience of candidates appearing in the examination, several unreserved special trains will also be operated on the Banaras-Ballia, Azamgarh-Ballia, and Ballia-Azamgarh routes. These trains will make it easier to reach examination centres from the districts of Purvanchal. Some regular trains will be affected The railway administration has informed that in view of the operation of special trains, the timings of some regular trains have been changed. Candidates will get major relief Railway officials say that a large number of candidates are likely to travel for the UP Police Constable recruitment examination. Keeping this in view, special trains are being operated connecting major cities of Purvanchal, including Gorakhpur, Lucknow, Varanasi, Azamgarh, and Ballia, so that examinees do not have to face the crowd and travel-related problems.

stories.title: Some had wrong names, others found gender changed in marksheets:Over 4,000 UP board students have applied; marksheets will take time to arrive
stories.summary: UP Board students may have to wait longer for their corrected results, as thousands have applied for changes in their marksheets. A total of 4,697 applications have been received from around 10 districts under the Varanasi regional office. The requests involve various types of corrections, including errors in students' names, parents' names, date of birth, gender, and photographs. In several cases, students found mistakes in their own names, while others reported incorrect entries for their mother’s or father’s names. Some students also discovered that their gender had been recorded incorrectly. According to officials, the highest number of applications- 1,275, is for name corrections. This is followed by 1,139 applications for changes in fathers' names, 974 for mothers' names, and 786 for date-of-birth corrections. Additionally, 92 students have applied to correct wrongly recorded gender details, while 431 applications have been submitted for changes in photographs. The large number of correction requests is expected to delay the processing of updated marksheets and related results. Applications were taken from students till May 12 UP Board had released the examination results of 10th and 12th students on April 23. Errors were found in the online marksheets of many students. The board had sought applications from students to get these corrected. Applications were filled within the stipulated time frame by the DIOS of all districts. The last applications were submitted on May 12. This is why marksheets are likely to arrive by the end of June. Most applications for corrections have come from the Azamgarh district. From here, there are a total of 905 applications for High School and Intermediate. Among these, there are 696 applications for High School and 209 for Intermediate. Similarly, from Ballia, there are a total of 766 applications combining both classes, and 702 applications from Ghazipur. The least number of applications is from Varanasi with 237, and Sonbhadra with 207 applications. Marksheets will be issued after corrections Bhaskar Mishra, Regional Additional Secretary of the Board of Secondary Education, Varanasi, informed that applications for corrections have been obtained from the DIOS of districts and uploaded on the board's site. Marksheets will be issued after corrections. Marksheets are likely to be issued by the end of this month. Every effort is being made to ensure that there is no error in any marksheet.

stories.title: From ₹200 for his first song to concerts nationwide:Kashmiri singer says, 'Lucknow's biryani is delicious, Kashmir is peaceful'
stories.summary: Baabarr Mudacer, who earned just ₹200 for his first song, has emerged as one of Kashmir's rising musical talents and now performs concerts across the country. Known for his versatility in Sufi, rap, classical, and soulful melodies, he has performed in major cities including Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata. His passion for singing grew so strong that he left his studies in 2012 to pursue music. Since entering the mainstream music scene in 2018, he has steadily built a loyal fan base. Mudacer performed in Lucknow on June 6 and received an enthusiastic response from fans. Expressing his fondness for the city, he said, “I love Lucknow. The biryani here is delicious. I also had matka kulfi, which was excellent.” Speaking about his home state, Kashmir, he said that peace prevails there. During his second visit to Lucknow, Mudacer spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about his musical journey, career struggles, favourite singers and rappers, his affection for Lucknow, and his views on the killing of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moose Wala. Read the conversation... Question- When did your singing journey begin, and when did you first discover your passion for music? Answer- It started in my childhood. I have always been passionate about singing. Over time, that passion grew stronger, turned into an obsession, and eventually became my profession. Music has been an inseparable part of my life since my early years, and I share a deep emotional connection with singing. Question- Your mother once mentioned in an interview that your first earnings from singing was ₹200. Can you tell us the full story behind that? Answer- In first grade, I went on a picnic with my school teacher and classmates. All the children were sitting in a circle. I was asked to get up and sing there. I always used to get up. The school people also knew that I had more interest in singing. And when I sang there, a tourist was sitting in front. He was very happy and gave me a reward of ₹200. Question- What challenges do artists from Jammu-Kashmir face? Answer- Yes, see, first of all, an artist needs a platform. Artists from Kashmir emerge independently. Everyone works hard on their own. There is no government support for them. I want the government to provide some support so that upcoming budding artists don't have to face the difficulties that we have faced. Question- Did you face criticism in the early days? Answer- There were many challenges. Difficulties are a part of every profession, but when you choose a career that is uncertain, the criticism tends to be greater. My family opposed my decision when I was young, and society had its doubts as well. People will always have something to say; that is their nature. I learned not to be distracted by it. The key is to keep working hard, stay focused on your goal, and leave the rest to Allah. Question- Do you enjoy singing alone in valleys of Kashmir more, or performing before large audience? Answer- Singing in the valleys of Kashmir and performing before a crowd are two completely different experiences. Sometimes, when I am alone, I head to the hills and spend some time there. It helps me refresh myself because constant shows, travelling, and work can be exhausting. Everyone needs moments of peace and a change of atmosphere, and I find that calm and rejuvenation in the valleys of Kashmir. Question- What is your favorite song? Answer- I have many favourite songs, and it largely depends on my mood. When I'm travelling in the car, I usually listen to rap. If I'm sitting in the mountains, I prefer listening to ghazals. My musical preferences change with the moment and the setting. That's why it's a difficult question to answer, I can't pick just one favourite song. Question- Your song 'Mera Dil Ye Pukare Aaja...' sung in high notes received a lot of praise on social media. Did you feel you were getting a new identity? Answer- No, no. Things had already started before that. This song was actually sung by Lata ji a long time ago, so this song was very close to my heart. I just recorded it casually, and it went viral across the globe, so this song gave me a push. I am very grateful to the people. This song always makes people recognize me, saying, "This is the same person. You sang that song." Wherever I go, wherever I travel, people recognize me. All thanks to Lata ji and all the old composers and those who wrote this song. Thank you very much to everyone. Also, thanks to the new generation. They liked this song more in my voice. Question- You have been given the title of Mad Rockstar. How do you view this title? Answer- Yes, MAD stands for Music And Donate. I try to help people in my own way as much as I can. That's why people call me that, and I like it. A person should help someone through their art because if you have come into this world, then helping each other is important. Question- What do you like about the flavors of Lucknow? Answer- I’ve tried the biryani here, and I really like it. In fact, when I arrived in Lucknow yesterday, the first thing I had was biryani. I also tasted the famous matka kulfi in the evening after we landed. It was delicious; they make it really well here. Question- You are a favorite of many people. Who is your favorite singer? Answer- Very difficult question. A person doesn't have just one favorite singer, ... so currently there are 2, 4, 5 names. Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan Sahab, Jagjit Singh Sahab, Ghulam Ali Sahab, Mehandi Ali Sahab, and there are also two-four rappers like Sidhu Moose Wala ji was. Question- How much regret is there about Sidhu Moosewala ji's passing? Answer- Very much. It's a big loss. It was a huge loss. He was the only son of his parents, and his death was also a major setback for the Punjabi music industry. Every artist is unique; someone like him comes only once. Another artist may emerge, but they will have their own distinct identity. Sidhu Moose Wala's loss cannot truly be replaced. Such incidents are tragic and should not happen.

stories.title: Haryanvi dancer seeks justice after on-stage molestation:FIR filed in Hathras, says ‘I want to eliminate such beasts’
stories.summary: A Haryanvi dancer has demanded strict action against a youth accused of molesting her during a stage performance in Uttar Pradesh's Hathras district. Based on her complaint, police at Sasni police station have registered an FIR against an unidentified accused under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The incident took place on June 3 during a birthday celebration where the dancer was performing. She reached Hathras on Sunday and recorded her statement before police. A video of the incident had earlier gone viral on social media. ‘This fight is for all artists’ In a video released after the controversy, the dancer said her fight was not only for herself but for all women and artists who face harassment during public performances. “This fight is not just about my self-respect but for all those girls and artists who face such incidents. I want justice and will fight for it,” she said. She added that she was seeking justice for every woman who faces misconduct at public events and stage shows. ‘I want to end such beasts’ The dancer appealed to society to support women facing harassment. “If society stands with a daughter, no one can harm her. Today it is me; tomorrow it could be your daughter. I do not want to end myself. I want to end such beasts,” she said. Responding to online trolling, she said stage performances are her livelihood and help support her family. “I do not dance on stage as a hobby. I do this work to run my household. If money was my only concern, my sister, who is more beautiful than me, would also be in this profession,” she said. How the incident unfolded According to the dancer, the accused first approached her during the performance and allegedly tried to put money inside her dress in an inappropriate manner. She later shared a video of the incident on social media. She alleged that the youth returned to the stage during another performance and touched her waist. The dancer then slapped him on stage and confronted him in front of the audience. Videos of both incidents circulated widely on social media, triggering public debate and calls for action against the accused. Police are now investigating the case and trying to identify the youth seen in the viral videos.
