stories.title: Sacred thread cut off from hand, stopped from worshipping:Reporter goes undercover as labourer to expose UP conversion network
stories.summary: “If you want Jesus’ prayer to have an effect, you must remove the sacred thread tied around your wrist. Otherwise, your troubles will never go away. And yes, stay away from worship.” This was said to a Dainik Bhaskar reporter during an alleged brainwashing session aimed at religious conversion. In Uttar Pradesh, people are allegedly being persuaded to change their faith with promises of relief from illness, poverty and personal hardships. Dainik Bhaskar received information about secret churches operating in Lakhimpur district. These centres reportedly have no signboards and display no images of Jesus. To avoid attracting police attention, the process is no longer referred to as conversion; instead, organisers call it “Grahan” (acceptance). To expose what is claimed to be a large-scale conversion network operating along the India-Nepal border, the Dainik Bhaskar team went undercover. The reporters disguised themselves as labourers and worked in fields for 20 days. During this period, the group made contact with them. Hidden-camera recordings allegedly revealed multiple layers of the network. Seven stages of conversion revealed When the reporter entered the alleged conversion network, seven stages of the process emerged. In Part 1 of this investigation, we explain the first three stages. Stage 1: Winning trust through local contacts The team reached Dalrajpur village in Lakhimpur district disguised as labourers. They searched for work within a 4-km radius and eventually found employment at a farmhouse. A hut was provided for accommodation. While working there, they gradually built relationships with local residents. The reporters spoke about their supposed hardships, claiming they were poor and suffering from illness. Before long, this information allegedly reached Pastor Vijay, a Christian cleric originally from Nepal. According to locals, he has been active in the area for around 30 years and operates a secret church from his home. His associates allegedly identify poor and sick individuals and encourage them to visit him. On the tenth day, a group of labourers advised the reporters to meet Pastor Vijay. A visit to his secret church was arranged for Sunday morning at 8 am. Stage 2: Emotional persuasion through personal testimonies The reporters arrived at the church at the appointed time. Pastor Vijay seated them beside him and remained silent for a while before beginning a conversation. Pastor Vijay- So, what is your problem? Reporter- We work at the farmhouse. Problems keep coming one after another. Our whole family has suffered because of them. I cannot get rid of my addiction. My left hand does not lift properly. We never manage to save any money. We even had to sell our land. Pastor Vijay- You have come to the place where the path opens. The Lord says in His word that whoever comes near Him, He comes near them. The Lord stays close to those whose lives are full of troubles. To reinforce the message, Pastor Vijay called over two more people, government school teacher Shivprasad Gautam and his wife. Pastor Vijay- This is our teacher. For two to four years, his life was full of difficulties. He wasted ₹12–13 lakh because of his problems. Whatever he earned from his job went into that. Then he came closer to the Lord, and all those problems disappeared. Pastor Vijay then showed passages from his mobile phone. Government Teacher Shivprasad Gautam- You have come to the right place because we wander only as much as is written in our destiny. Pastor Vijay- You do not need to worry. If you have any problem, we can even pray for you over the phone. Reporter- Will I need to come here again? Pastor Vijay- Yes, you will have to come once or twice more. Shivprasad’s Wife- Do not worry. You will recover. Consider yourself to be sitting in God’s house.” Reporter- Okay. Shivprasad’s Wife- A Baba is coming from Nepal. It would be good if he listens to your problem. It may take him some time to arrive. You are not in a hurry, are you? Reporter- No. Pastor Vijay- Come and sit closer to us. He then placed his hand on the reporter’s head and asked him to repeat a prayer. Pastor Vijay- Repeat after me: Lord, we come to your refuge. I surrender my life to you. Reporter- Lord, we come to your refuge. I surrender my life to you. Stage 3: Asking followers to abandon Hindu symbols and practices Once the group appeared satisfied that the reporter had accepted their message, they moved to the next stage. The reporter was told that Jesus’ prayers would not work unless Hindu religious symbols and practices were abandoned. Shivprasad’s Wife- You have not worn any amulets or anything, have you? Reporter- A worship ceremony was performed about a month ago. That is when this sacred thread was tied. Shivprasad’s Wife- If you remove this thread, the prayers we offer will reach you. Otherwise, it will cause harm. It is linked to ritual practices. Please remove it. We also used to observe fasts. When prayers were offered for us, they would not reach us. Pastor Vijay- (Pointing towards Shivprasad) He once told me there was nothing left in his house. But my Lord told me there was still a lot there. We went to his house and started opening cupboards and storage spaces. Things kept emerging. Shivprasad’s Wife- There was also water kept there. What kind of water was it? Was it from Haridwar? Reporter- Do you mean Ganga water from Haridwar or Prayagraj? Shivprasad’s Wife- Yes. That water was blocking the prayer. Pastor Vijay- Our objective is that prayer should not stop anywhere. If it connects, it should connect completely. Shivprasad’s Wife- (To the pastor) Weren’t you noticing? While praying, he was making ‘foen-foen’ sounds. The prayer was becoming ineffective. Pastor Vijay- He was under a very dangerous influence. Even petrol and diesel could not burn the ‘jantu’. Reporter- What is a ‘jantu’? Others Present- Amulets and such things. Pastor Vijay- In our language, we call all these things ‘jantu’. During the conversation, someone brought a blade. Pastor Vijay then cut the sacred thread from the reporter’s wrist and said they would keep it. What has the investigation revealed so far? According to the findings of the undercover investigation-

stories.title: “They are psychopaths”: Matt Walsh erupts after Jesse Ridgway and Ashley end pregnancy over Down syndrome diagnosis
stories.summary: YouTuber Jesse Ridgway and his wife Ashley revealed that they ended a pregnancy after receiving a Down syndrome diagnosis for their unborn child. The announcement led to heavy criticism from political commentator Matt Walsh, who condemned their decision on X. Ridgway defended the choice, calling the experience traumatic and saying the couple believed it was best for their family.

stories.title: CJP’s NEET stir today, Youth Congress rejects overture
stories.summary: Newly formed online group Cockroach Janta Party sought coordination with the Indian Youth Congress for its upcoming NEET protest, but the overture was rejected. The IYC stated it will not share platforms and is conducting its own nationwide protests, focusing on government accountability. Congress strategists remain skeptical of CJP's sudden emergence.

stories.title: Facing desertion by MPs, Mamata Banerjee clips Abhishek’s wings
FIR filed against ‘Khan Sir’ in coaching centre firing case
Expedite verifications, MEA tells Dhaka
stories.summary: India has urged Bangladesh to expedite the verification of suspected illegal immigrants to facilitate their deportation. The MEA highlighted an existing bilateral mechanism for this process, emphasizing that once nationality is verified, deportation can proceed smoothly. India reiterated that laws are in place to address individuals staying illegally in the country.

stories.title: Oil India strikes natural gas in third Andaman offshore well
stories.summary: State-run Oil India Limited (OIL) has announced the discovery of natural gas in its third exploratory well, Vijayapuram-3, located off the Andaman Islands. This finding further strengthens the hydrocarbon potential of the region, with gas confirmed through continuous flaring and pressure build-up. OIL has now established hydrocarbon presence in two of its three wells in the Andaman offshore block.

stories.title: Great Nicobar Project isn't about defence: Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi released a video of his Nicobar visit, calling the Great Nicobar Project a "lie" and alleging it benefits a businessman for hotels and casinos. He initiated an online petition, "we choose green over greed," urging Indians to protect the island's ecosystem and tribal communities from destruction.

stories.title: No mass data leak: JEE (Advanced) authorities
stories.summary: JEE (Advanced) authorities have clarified that a cloud storage misconfiguration identified by an ethical hacker did not lead to any mass extraction of candidate data. IIT-Roorkee stated the issue, which occurred during technical interventions, was immediately rectified and access was restricted, with no impact on examination records or results.

stories.title: BJP cites GDP figures, says joke’s on Rahul
Blood test can predict lung cancer 5 years before diagnosis
stories.summary: Scientists found blood markers that can predict lung cancer more than five years in advance. This breakthrough could help detect the disease early in India, where most cases are found late. A 14-protein signature in blood identified individuals at higher risk. This finding may lead to earlier monitoring and preventive measures for lung cancer.

stories.title: Bangladesh border guards, BSF accuse each other of push-in attempts
stories.summary: Border Guard Bangladesh accused India's BSF of attempting to push over 70 individuals into Bangladesh near Lalmonirhat, Naogaon, and Chapainawabganj. Meanwhile, BSF reported thwarting a BGB attempt to help 10 Bangladeshis enter India. Both forces disowned stranded individuals, leading to heightened border patrols.

stories.title: SC: Can’t use OSA to deny accused access to documents relied on by prosecution
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that an accused's right to a fair trial includes access to prosecution documents, even if classified under the Official Secrets Act. The court ordered the government to provide highly confidential documents to retired Major General V.K. Singh, facing charges for revealing secrets in his book, emphasizing fair trial rights.

stories.title: Over $580,000 forfeited in Australian visa fraud crackdown; man jailed for submitting false migration documents
Twitch star Nmplol breaks silence on divorce settlement with ex-wife Malena Tudi
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Nmplol has disclosed details of his divorce settlement with ex-wife Malena Tudi. The court finalized their marriage under a no-fault insupportability ruling, with most assets split 50/50, though Malena received a larger share of Starforge Systems. Nmplol also revealed incurring over $400,000 in legal fees and expressed relief that the lengthy process is finally over.

stories.title: Canadian man settles in India with wife's family: Cost of living way lower than Toronto, lost 14lbs in 5 months
PM Modi inspects indigenous defence systems at Surat facility, briefed about desi light tank Zorawar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Larsen & Toubro's Armed Systems Complex in Surat, reviewing advanced defence equipment and indigenous armoured vehicles. He was briefed on 'Zorawar', India's first indigenous light battle tank designed for mountainous terrains and rapid deployment along the LAC.

stories.title: Nick Polom reaches divorce agreement with Malena Tudi following $400,000 legal battle but one settlement detail grabs attention
stories.summary: Nick Polom, better known as Nmplol, has finalized his no-fault divorce from fellow streamer Malena Tudi. According to Dexerto, most assets were divided equally, while Starforge Systems received separate treatment. The court also denied Tudi’s request for monthly spousal support. The outcome has sparked online debate about alimony, asset division, and the financial cost of public breakups.

stories.title: KSI’s departure from Sidemen triggers fresh debate after group releases clarifying statement
stories.summary: The Sidemen have released a statement following KSI’s departure from the group. While they said they respect his decision, they revealed that the announcement came before a mutual plan had been agreed upon. The group hoped to organize a proper farewell but said events unfolded differently. Despite the change, the remaining members confirmed they will continue creating content together.

stories.title: JiDion rejects Alex Rosen partnership after his $10,000 ChudTheBuilder bond contribution raises questions
stories.summary: YouTuber JiDion has ended his partnership with Alex Rosen after Rosen donated $10,000 toward the bond of Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder. Speaking to followers, JiDion said the money could have supported more meaningful causes and called the donation unacceptable. The controversy has sparked widespread discussion online and brought renewed attention to both creators.

stories.title: Epstein's prison guard reveals shocking details about day he was found dead in his cell
Cloudburst, flashfloods damaged houses in J&K’s Reasi
stories.summary: Flashfloods from a cloudburst in Reasi's Bathoi village on Thursday caused significant damage to homes and blocked roads with mudslides. Fortunately, no injuries or fatalities were reported. This marks the fifth such event in the Jammu region recently. Authorities are providing immediate assistance to affected families, while adverse weather also led to the suspension of pilgrimages in Kishtwar.

stories.title: Ladakh women’s group slams liquor sale nod, warns of stir
stories.summary: Ladakh's Buddhist women's wing is strongly opposing the Union Territory's new excise policy allowing liquor sales, fearing it will worsen social issues like drug abuse and domestic violence. They advocate for stricter drug control and warn of protests if the policy isn't reconsidered, emphasizing women's role in preserving the region's social fabric.

stories.title: Henry Nowak won't be the last: JD Vance blames mass migration for UK stabbing, triggers diplomatic row
Save Soil–Cauvery Calling: Farmers' income jumps from Rs 30,000 to Rs 3 lakh per acre
stories.summary: A tree-based farming model by Save Soil–Cauvery Calling is transforming agriculture, boosting incomes from Rs 30,000 to Rs 2.5–3 lakh per acre. This ecological solution, accredited by UN bodies, has empowered farmers like Valluvan, enhancing soil health and crop yields. The movement aims to plant 242 crore trees, supporting hundreds of thousands of farmers with extensive training and resources.

stories.title: TMC huddle at Mamata Banerjee's residence: 8 of 80 MLAs turn up amid party split concerns
US judge invalidates travel and visa ban on 39 countries: What happens next?
Indian student fights for life in Chicago after 25-ft fall at subway station, family seeks help
‘Gurdwara is empty’: Sikhs scared to come out of houses after Vickrum Digwa killed Henry Nowak
NTPC to set up flexible coal-fired units to ensure reliable power supply
stories.summary: NTPC is setting up flexible coal-fired thermal power units to balance intermittent renewable energy generation and ensure grid stability. These sub-critical units, designed for two-shift operation and lower minimum loads, will provide crucial balancing support as renewable energy's share grows, reinforcing India's energy transition.

stories.title: 'Anna' movement in Tamil Nadu BJP: Mass resignations leave party staring at an exodus
Unicorn in the USA: Indians aren't stealing American jobs; they are building entire HR departments
stories.summary: Immigrants are driving America's innovation, founding 59% of billion-dollar startups, known as unicorns. People of Indian origin lead this trend, establishing 96 such companies. These ventures employ thousands and contribute trillions to the U.S. economy, challenging narratives of immigrants harming the job market. International students also play a crucial role in this entrepreneurial surge.

stories.title: 'Carry Tiranga, apply sunscreen, stay hydrated': Cockroach Janta Party shares protest itinerary; makes appeal to PM Modi
Saudi Arabia launches new Jeddah–India shipping link to boost trade flows
YouTubers face backlash for terminating pregnancy after learning child had Down syndrome
Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, an ace fighter and experienced test pilot, appointed IAF vice chief
stories.summary: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, a seasoned fighter and test pilot, has been appointed the next Vice Chief of the Air Staff, effective July 1. His extensive experience in operational roles, indigenous fighter projects, and aircraft testing brings significant expertise to the IAF's leadership. He previously served as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff, contributing to jointness among defense forces.

stories.title: Punjab to roll out monthly aid for women under Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna from July 1
New rule for work permit in US: Asylum seekers may lose jobs under DHS proposal
Fuel-saving push, rising costs: Is public transport affordable enough?
Drug smugglers Baltej Singh and Himatjit Kahlon lose final bid to overturn jail terms in NZ
Whistling Woods International: Shaping the next generation of creative professionals
8L volunteers within hours: Annamalai's 'political movement' becomes an instant hit
Henry Nowak case: How handcuffed UK student's murder by Sikh man sparked national outrage - timeline of events
He feared he couldn't compete with AI: Indian family dumps American Dream, leaves US after tragedy
'People's anger forced Cong to change CM in Karnataka': PM Modi
'Are you from India?' Donald Trump takes swipe at reporter in Oval office, triggers racism row
stories.summary: During a White House press interaction, President Trump questioned an Indian journalist's nationality before taking her question, later stating he was "kidding." He then described Indian Prime Minister Modi as a "good friend" and expressed confidence in a trade agreement, asserting the US now benefits significantly from its economic ties with India.

stories.title: CBSE denies 'data breach' despite repeated cyber attacks for past 3 days; files complaint
Evening news wrap: India's GDP growth beats expectations in final quarter; K Annamalai launches new political movement & more
Karmelo Anthony trial: Attorney says he stabbed Austin Metcalf in defense, didn't attack anyone else
'Pakistan must vacate': India slams election plans in PoK's Gilgit-Baltistan assembly
World's first AI-designed vaccine developed by UK scientists enters human trials
stories.summary: A groundbreaking AI-designed vaccine for Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever has entered human trials, marking a world-first for medical research. Developed by Oxford University and Basecamp Research, this initiative showcases AI's potential to drastically accelerate vaccine development for emerging infectious diseases. The trial aims to assess safety and immune response, potentially ushering in a new era of AI-assisted medicine.

stories.title: 'Leaving with my head held high': Mamata aide Firhad Hakim resigns as Kolkata mayor
'Give me one last chance': Indian man confronted in UK over alleged grooming of 14-year-old girl
Annamalai launches 'political movement' after quitting BJP: All you need to know about 'We The Leaders'
UAE makes history with launch of first ever licensed sports betting and iGaming platform
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has launched its first licensed online gaming platform, Play971. This marks a significant step in the country's regulated gaming industry. The platform offers sports wagering and internet gaming options. Users must be 21 and present in the UAE. This development signals a new era for regulated commercial gaming in the nation.

stories.title: In 1930s, Australia released cane toads to fight beetles; today 200 million have taken over the country
Quote of the day by Chinese philosopher Confucius: “Attack the evil that is within yourself, rather than attacking...”
Another regional force crumbling: How TMC is going the Shiv Sena, NCP way
'I was in office that was attacked': Iran top diplomat Araghchi recalls Khamenei's 'martyrdom'
'Don't want to burden top leadership': What Annamalai told BJP in his resignation letter
stories.summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has resigned to launch a new political movement, aiming to end "cult and dynastic" politics. Annamalai expressed a desire to change the notion of politics and connect with local aspirations, stating national parties often fail to speak the language of Tamil Nadu's people.

stories.title: Was there a hidden river under the Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt: New evidence rewrites history
UK tightens student visa rules as universities face ban over international student visa abuse
stories.summary: UK universities face stricter rules for recruiting international students to combat visa system abuse. New government plans demand higher compliance standards, with tougher targets for visa refusal, enrolment, and course completion rates. Institutions failing to meet these benchmarks risk recruitment restrictions or losing sponsorship licenses, aiming to ensure genuine study purposes.

stories.title: Bihar government withdraws Lalu Yadav, Rabri Devi's Z-plus security cover
stories.summary: Explaining the category that has been withdrawn, an official said, “The Z-plus security comprises a dedicated team of trained personnel equipped with advanced arms.” Despite the downgrade, Lalu Prasad and Rabri Devi will continue to receive security support. Their present arrangements include between two and eight BSAP house guards, two bodyguards from the Patna District Force, along with a pilot vehicle and a bulletproof car.

stories.title: PM Modi welcomes AirTrunk's Rs 3 lakh crore investment plan in India, highlights digital economy push
stories.summary: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk plans a massive Rs 3 lakh crore investment in India by 2030 to boost digital infrastructure, including data centres and AI capacity. Prime Minister Modi welcomed the move, highlighting its potential to strengthen India's global position in cloud computing and AI, create jobs, and drive innovation-led growth.

stories.title: More trouble brewing for Mamata's TMC? Expelled MLA Ritabrata Banerjee makes fresh claim
stories.summary: Expelled TMC leader Ritabrata Banerjee expressed confidence that support for his rebel faction will grow, claiming a significant number of MLAs are backing him. He also appealed to CM Suvendu Adhikari to take action against BJP leader Priyanka Tibrewal for protesting outside a fellow rebel's residence.

stories.title: 'Cannot work against conscience': What Ramalinga said after quitting DKS cabinet
stories.summary: Announcing his decision in Bengaluru, Reddy said he could not continue in the ministry after chief minister DK Shivakumar allegedly failed to honour an assurance made to him regarding the key portfolio. "The resignation comes at a time when Rahul Gandhi is in town. I cannot work against my conscience, so I am resigning as minister," said Reddy.

stories.title: 'There is no loss': Tamil Nadu BJP chief as his predecessor Annamalai quits party
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagendran dismissed any loss following K. Annamalai's exit, who has launched a new political movement, the APJ Abdul Kalam Centre for Ethics and Politics. Annamalai aims to foster systemic change, ending cult and dynastic politics, and encouraging technocrats. His departure follows speculation after the BJP's performance in recent elections.

stories.title: India’s 100th wetland, Surha Tal of Balia, enters the global list of Ramsar site
Congress MP Digvijaya Singh seeks white paper on NTA exam irregularities; writes to PM Modi
stories.summary: Addressing the troubling trends in examination management, Congress MP Digvijaya Singh has requested Prime Minister Modi to issue a comprehensive white paper on the National Testing Agency's irregularities spanning eight years. Highlighting the recent NEET-UG 2026 cancellation, Singh expressed the growing anxiety among students stemming from unresolved leak issues.

stories.title: 'In best of families...': Netanyahu responds to Trump's 'crazy' remark, acknowledges 'tactical disagreements'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu acknowledged 'tactical disagreements' with US President Trump over regional conflicts but emphasized their shared goals, particularly countering Iran's nuclear ambitions and Hezbollah. Despite recent heated exchanges, Netanyahu hailed Trump as Israel's 'greatest friend,' citing his strong support for the nation. Both leaders aim for regional stability.

stories.title: Annamalai parts ways with BJP: What may have led to exit of its most prominent Tamil Nadu leader
stories.summary: Throughout his tenure, Annamalai distinguished himself through relentless attacks on Dravidian politics and the leaders who shaped it. His criticism was not restricted to political opponents. Even while the BJP was aligned with the AIADMK, he repeatedly targeted figures from the ally's camp, creating friction within the alliance and widening differences between the two parties.

stories.title: DK Shivakumar goes into damage-control mode after 'closest of friend' Ramalinga Reddy's cabinet exit in Karnataka
stories.summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar has assured that there is "nothing to worry" regarding the resignation of minister Ramalinga Reddy. Reddy, a close friend and senior leader, expressed dissatisfaction with his allocated portfolio and sought a different ministerial post. Shivakumar stated he would discuss the matter with Reddy to resolve the issue.

stories.title: IMD weather alert: Heavy rain, thunderstorms forecast across multiple states this week
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department is predicting an impressive surge of the southwest monsoon, which will unleash a wave of rain, thunderstorms, and brisk winds across the country. South India, including Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, is set to experience intense to extreme rainfall.

stories.title: Switzerland is building the world’s largest underground battery that could power 210,000 homes for a day
'Leaving my fate in the hands of Constitution': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke heads to India
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke is en route to India for a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Dipke cites alleged irregularities in national examinations like NEET and CUET, impacting millions of students. He plans a peaceful, lawful demonstration after arriving on June 6.

stories.title: Putin's word of caution on India-China ties; rejects notion that Pakistan is under Beijing's control
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated Moscow will not interfere in India-China relations, expressing confidence in Prime Minister Modi and President Xi resolving border disputes. Putin emphasized Russia's strong ties with both nations, asserting that its relationships do not negatively impact each other. He also highlighted potential defense cooperation with India.

stories.title: No woman in Karnataka cabinet: How CM DK Shivakumar responded to criticism
stories.summary: Responding to criticism from the BJP regarding the lack of women ministers, Shivakumar said, “Let them (BJP) wait; there are a lot of vacancies. Last time, too, there were no women in the first round. We are all there,” he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. Emphasising his party’s record on women’s welfare, he added, “We have set a model in the country.”

stories.title: 'I like your Prime Minister a lot': Donald Trump praises PM Modi as US-India trade talks continue
stories.summary: Momentum towards a deal has strengthened in recent weeks. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said the negotiations were nearing completion, with only a limited number of issues still unresolved. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has similarly indicated that most matters have been settled, with discussions now centred on finalising the remaining details before the first phase of the agreement is unveiled.

stories.title: Drug firms told to strengthen monitoring of medicine side effects
stories.summary: India's drug regulator has mandated pharmaceutical companies to establish robust systems for tracking and reporting adverse drug reactions. This directive, stemming from Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, reinforces the critical need for post-marketing surveillance to ensure patient safety. The move aligns with a global push for real-world safety data to identify rare or delayed side effects.

stories.title: We are no longer part of INDIA bloc: DMK
stories.summary: The DMK has declared its departure from the INDIA bloc, citing Congress's alleged betrayal after the assembly elections. Despite this, DMK MPs will continue to support other alliance members on matters of public interest. This decision follows Congress's alliance with the TVK-led government in Tamil Nadu, which DMK officials condemned as 'backstabbing'.

stories.title: Indian Army prepared for both short and intense conflicts; drones being integrated into every formation: Gen Dwivedi
stories.summary: Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi highlights lessons from Operation Sindoor, emphasizing integrated, technology-enabled warfare and the central role of drones. He stresses preparedness for multi-front conflicts and Pakistan's need to deter terror attacks, while also detailing the stable but sensitive situation along the LAC with China.

stories.title: Sherpa survives 6-day Everest ordeal sans food, O2
stories.summary: A 52-year-old Sherpa guide, Dawa 'Hillary' Sherpa, presumed dead on Mount Everest after vanishing on May 29, was miraculously found alive six days later near Base Camp. He survived over 12km of treacherous terrain without supplies, scavenging for sustenance after the climbing season ended and routes were dismantled.

stories.title: Constitution expert Subhash Kashyap dies at 97
stories.summary: Renowned constitutional law and parliamentary affairs expert Subhash C Kashyap passed away at 97. Kashyap, a former Lok Sabha secretary general and Padma Bhushan recipient, was a widely consulted authority on parliamentary procedures. His extensive writings on Parliament made him a significant figure in political science and law.

stories.title: Candace Owens shuts down presidential rumors while pushing Tucker Carlson into the 2028 conversation
stories.summary: Candace Owens said she has no interest in running for president in 2028 and joked that she would rather be a dictator. During an interview at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, she threw her support behind Tucker Carlson as a possible presidential candidate. Carlson has denied any plans to run, but speculation about his political future continues.

stories.title: ‘Complete probe in 6 weeks’: SC raps Gujarat Police for 20-year delay
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has strongly criticized Gujarat police for a 20-year-old investigation delay, ordering its completion within six weeks. Justices Karol and Masih emphasized constitutional courts cannot ignore such prolonged probes, especially when a complainant faces immense difficulty. The court highlighted the seriousness of lost case records, impacting the justice system and demanding swift action.

stories.title: DU assistant professor murdered at home in east Delhi
stories.summary: A 42-year-old Delhi University assistant professor, Debosmita Paul, was discovered murdered in her Vasundhara Enclave apartment. Her sister found her with severe head injuries, suggesting an attack with a blunt object and possibly a sharp weapon. While robbery isn't the primary suspect, investigators are exploring her personal and professional life, including ongoing separation proceedings.

stories.title: Chemotherapy drug supply crisis hits cancer care
stories.summary: Cancer patients in India are facing a critical shortage of life-saving chemotherapy drugs, Cisplatin and Carboplatin, disrupting treatment schedules. Hospitals report dwindling stocks, forcing patients to scramble for supplies. Doctors warn that prolonged unavailability of these essential medicines, with limited alternatives, could negatively impact patient outcomes and survival rates.

stories.title: 500 ethanol pumps by year-end: Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri
stories.summary: India is set to significantly expand its ethanol dispensing stations, with 500 planned by December and 5,000 by 2027, to boost flex-fuel vehicle adoption. This initiative, marked by the launch of Maruti Suzuki's WagonR flex-fuel car, aims to reduce fuel imports. The government is implementing supportive measures including pricing incentives and infrastructure development.

stories.title: Rahul: Youth paying for broken system
Government mulls cement roads amid bitumen price spike
stories.summary: Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari is exploring cement concrete roads over bituminous ones due to a surge in bitumen prices and supply disruptions from the West Asia conflict. He also highlighted the potential of domestically produced bio-bitumen from rice straw and other biowaste to reduce imports and save foreign exchange.

stories.title: IRCTC disables 3cr user IDs, flags 6cr; scales up AI-based kitchen monitoring
stories.summary: IRCTC has taken significant steps to combat ticket booking fraud by deactivating over three crore suspicious user IDs and placing another six crore under verification. To enhance food safety, the railway's catering arm has expanded its AI-based kitchen monitoring system, utilizing over 2,300 cameras to detect hygiene violations.

stories.title: Mallikarjun Kharge among 7 Congress nominees for Rajya Sabha polls
stories.summary: The Congress party has announced seven candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge will contest from Karnataka, alongside Mansoor Ali Khan and Pawan Khera. Other nominations include Pranav Jha from Jharkhand, Praveen Chakravarty from Tamil Nadu, Meenakshi Natarajan from MP, and Neeraj Dangi from Rajasthan.

stories.title: India, UK launch initiatives for minerals, maritime cooperation
stories.summary: India and the UK have launched a Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory and signed an MoU for a Regional Maritime Security Centre of Excellence during UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper's visit. The two nations also reviewed progress in trade, technology, and defense, aiming to strengthen their future-oriented partnership.

stories.title: 'We are making lot of money with India': Trump claims trade gains have 'reversed'; praises PM Modi
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about reaching a trade agreement with India soon, stating that the previous trade imbalance has now reversed. Both nations have been engaged in constructive negotiations, aiming to finalize an interim trade pact while broader discussions continue. Despite ongoing talks, concerns remain regarding potential US tariffs on imports from several economies, including India.

stories.title: Japan PM may visit India next month for talks with PM Modi
Courts must not allow litigation to prolong decayed marriages: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that prolonged, broken marriages should not be prolonged by courts, citing the "foul sociological, psychological and mental hollowness" they create. Exercising its powers, the apex court dissolved a 15-year-old separation between two doctors, emphasizing marriage as a partnership of mutual respect and shared responsibility, not just a contract.

stories.title: “I regret doing it”: Sykkuno breaks silence on cheating controversy and shares emotional update on girlfriend
stories.summary: Sykkuno returned to Twitch on June 3, 2026, after a break following a cheating controversy. During his comeback stream, he admitted that his actions toward his girlfriend were “horrible” and said he spent months trying to repair their relationship. He shared that they are now happier together, thanked supporters, and said the experience helped him grow.

stories.title: Compassionate job for married daughter’s son? SC to rule
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will examine if a married daughter's son is eligible for compassionate employment after her father's death. This follows a recent ruling granting such rights to dependent married daughters. The Chhattisgarh government has been asked to respond to a petition challenging its denial of employment to a grandson.

stories.title: Not talking for a few days is not marital cruelty: SC acquits man convicted after wife’s suicide
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that a husband cannot be convicted of cruelty under Section 498A of the IPC solely for not speaking to his wife for a few days.

stories.title: El Nino is here, says European agency amid Pacific warming
stories.summary: The European weather agency has indicated El Nino has set in, with Pacific Ocean temperatures crossing the 0.5°C threshold in May. This development is expected to influence global weather patterns, including the Indian monsoon. While official declaration requires persistence, atmospheric changes are already being observed.

stories.title: Venezuela, a big energy source, comes calling
stories.summary: India is bolstering its energy security by deepening ties with Venezuela, a top crude oil supplier. Discussions between PM Modi and Venezuela's acting President focused on long-term energy contracts and cooperation in critical minerals, tech, and agriculture. This move diversifies India's oil sources amidst global supply chain challenges.

stories.title: Monsoon arrives in Kerala, after 3-day delay
stories.summary: India's crucial southwest monsoon has officially arrived in Kerala, three days later than anticipated. This marks the start of the four-month rainy season vital for agriculture. While the forecast was slightly off, the India Meteorological Department expects the monsoon to advance further across the country in the coming days, bringing much-needed rainfall.

stories.title: Buzz of cabinet reshuffle grows: 2 Union ministers don't figure among BJP's 1 1 Rajya Sabha picks
stories.summary: BJP's Rajya Sabha candidate list omits Union ministers Ravneet Singh Bittu and George Kurian, fueling cabinet reshuffle speculation. Notably, no outgoing MPs were renominated, with organizational functionaries securing berths. The party is yet to announce candidates from Jharkhand and Karnataka, leaving room for potential ministerial retention.

stories.title: YouTuber Jesse Ridgway says he and wife made difficult choice after fetal Down syndrome diagnosis
stories.summary: YouTuber Jesse Ridgway and his wife Ashley shared a difficult personal update. They learned their unborn child had Down syndrome during pregnancy. This led to a deeply emotional decision. The couple is now focusing on recovery and supporting each other. They expressed gratitude for fan support during this challenging time. Ridgway detailed the medical considerations that influenced their choice.

stories.title: Ex-wife of a Dubai prince 'abducted' amid bitter custody battle, lawyer raises alarm: 'She just vanished'
4.5-inch stab to the neck: Drunk man jailed over fatal attack on Saudi student in England
"I almost lost my eye": Pokimane opens up about painful medical scare
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Pokimane experienced a sudden and severe eye issue just before her birthday trip to Paris. An eyelash lodged in her tear duct caused intense pain and redness, nearly making her miss her flight. The rare condition surprised her doctor, but the eyelash was successfully removed, allowing her to travel.

stories.title: Perception of bias against minorities propaganda aimed at tarnishing India’s image: Rijiju
stories.summary: Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju dismissed claims of discrimination against minorities in India as propaganda and a malicious campaign. He highlighted a significant increase in the ministry's budget over the past decade, from Rs 1,949 crore to Rs 4,115 crore, as evidence of the government's commitment.

stories.title: New bill by Chip Roy targeting H-1Bs wants to end lottery, OPT: Put America's white-collar workers first
NC’s rebel MP Mehdi says he will join Delhi protest for J&K statehood, Art 370; calls for broader movement
stories.summary: National Conference plans a New Delhi protest for statehood and "constitutional guarantees," believed to refer to Article 370. Rebel MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi expressed willingness to join, urging a broader movement and outreach to opposition parties for sustained public support in the Valley.

stories.title: Vickrum Digwa's grandmother breaks silence on Henry Nowak's murder, defends killer's mother
Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr.: “True peace is not merely the absence of tension; it is…”
Auburn University student goes missing in Japan during family vacation, had a fight with mom over use of ChatGPT
UP CM Yogi orders inspection of hotels, commercial establishments after Delhi's Malviya Nagar fire tragedy
stories.summary: Following a fatal fire in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered comprehensive security inspections of hotels and commercial establishments across the state. Officials from multiple departments are tasked with ensuring fire safety systems are in place, with hotels required to submit audit reports. Strict legal action is threatened against violators.

stories.title: ‘Useless to try to pressure PM Modi’: Putin on US efforts to derail India-Russia ties
stories.summary: Russian President Putin reassured that India's growing US ties won't harm its long-standing relationship with Russia. He dismissed attempts to pressure New Delhi, highlighting India's robust economic growth and predicting a significant expansion in bilateral trade, aiming for $100 billion in the coming years. Putin expressed confidence in continued strong economic engagement.

stories.title: 'Don't come to airport': CJP founder's new appeal to supporters - what prompted U-turn?
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged supporters not to gather at Delhi Airport on 6 June, citing public and security concerns. Instead, he will seek permission at Parliament Street Police Station for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar demanding Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over examination controversies. The party also appointed Saurav Das, Vijeta Dahiya and Ashutosh Ranka as spokespersons.

stories.title: Miami real estate agent, ex-partner and two daughters found dead in murder-suicide
US lawmakers defy Trump in voting to end Iran war
stories.summary: Republican lawmakers are showing rare signs of independent thought, voting against President Trump's priorities on Capitol Hill. Recent acts of rebellion include opposing the Iran war without congressional authorization and blocking a controversial fund for alleged Biden administration overreach. While Trump's grip on the GOP remains strong, these small but noticeable tremors suggest a shift in congressional dynamics.

stories.title: DoPT plans IAS mentorship meet at statue of unity on Ekta Diwas
stories.summary: The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) has requested states and Union territories to nominate senior and young IAS officers for a mentorship and knowledge-sharing event at the Statue of Unity on Ekta Diwas. This initiative, inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's suggestion, aims to foster engagement and share expertise among civil servants.

stories.title: Sherpa survives 6-day Everest ordeal, crawls down 12km from 25k feet sans food, oxygen
Indian-Americans behind 96 billion-dollar startups in US, new study challenges rising hate
'I was simply told that...': RJD's Manoj Jha defends assisting CJP in holding presser at Constitution Club
'I can’t breathe': Why Henry Nowak's fatal stabbing by a Sikh man could become British Right's 'Black Lives Matter'
stories.summary: Like most memes that go viral on social media, it’s derivative and reductive, like a Yuval Harari offering. Whether it’s raining, how one reports said rain, and how one explains why it’s raining depends upon one’s availability heuristic, political leanings, scientific understanding, and even theological beliefs, or lack thereof.

stories.title: Starmer accuses Musk of ‘whipping up division’ over Henry Nowak's murder by Sikh man Vickrum Digwa
'Enduring strength of Sangh': Kumar Mangalam Birla lauds RSS for its century of service
stories.summary: Industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla lauded the RSS for its consistent societal and national support, highlighting its enduring strength in service and nation-building. Addressing a training camp, he also spoke of India's opportune moment amidst global shifts and the transformative impact of AI, stressing the need for national resilience during this critical development phase.

stories.title: 'I slowly started believing': Victim details alleged conversion push in TCS case chargesheet
stories.summary: A TCS employee in Nashik claims she was gradually convinced to convert to Islam to reduce mental stress, according to a police chargesheet. She alleges being encouraged to adopt Islamic practices, watch specific preachers, and was sexually exploited by an accused on a marriage promise. The chargesheet details extensive witness statements.

stories.title: Former NSA-turned-Trump critic, John Bolton to plead guilty over retaining classified documents: Report
stories.summary: John Bolton, former national security adviser to President Trump, is reportedly set to plead guilty to one felony count of illegally retaining classified documents. This plea agreement comes with a fine exceeding $2 million, as part of a case brought against him earlier this year in Maryland.

stories.title: Two Indian men claiming to be in same-sex relationship in NZ face deportation after...
'Cocaine-fuelled' Brit jailed for life over murder of Saudi student Mohammed Algasim in Cambridge
Bondi attack hero Ahmed al-Ahmed charged with assaulting father: Report
stories.summary: Ahmed al-Ahmed, lauded for disarming a Bondi Beach attacker, now faces assault charges. Police allege he assaulted his father in March. Al-Ahmed denies the claims, calling them 'fake information.' He was hailed a hero after the deadly shooting, receiving widespread praise and meeting the Prime Minister. The Bondi attack remains Australia's deadliest mass shooting since 1996.

stories.title: Rise of Ritabrata Banerjee: How ex-Left leader engineered Bengal's biggest political coup
stories.summary: Once a footnote in West Bengal politics, Ritabrata Banerjee has dramatically risen to become the Leader of Opposition after a sensational political shift. His journey from a CPI(M) expulsion to leading a rebellion within the TMC, now challenging the ruling party, has left the state's political landscape reeling.

stories.title: 'No resignation, no new party': Tamil Nadu BJP chief dismisses Annamalai exit buzz
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran has dismissed rumors of K Annamalai's resignation or plans to launch a new political outfit, stating there are no differences between them. This clarification follows intense speculation after Annamalai's meeting with Union Home Minister Amit Shah, fueled by reported disagreements over alliance strategies and Annamalai's desire to build the BJP as an independent force.

stories.title: Delayed wages in UAE: Payroll activity soars 151% as firms race to meet new salary deadline
Former US ambassador calls Indians corrupt, says America typically does not have fraud
IIT Roorkee's first BTech AI batch secures 100% placements
stories.summary: IIT-Roorkee's inaugural Data Science and AI BTech batch achieved 100% placements, with students securing roles at leading tech and finance firms like Amazon, Microsoft, and Goldman Sachs. The program, a collaboration with the Mehta Family Foundation, emphasizes practical AI development. This success highlights the growing demand for AI-skilled graduates.

stories.title: Indian man killed in Sharjah after alleged TikTok dispute turns into fatal attack
'Situation today pains me': Humayun Kabir offers Mamata Banerjee route back to Bengal assembly
stories.summary: AJUP founder Humayun Kabir has offered Mamata Banerjee a path back to the West Bengal Assembly from his Rejinagar constituency. Kabir, who won both Nowda and Rejinagar, stated he would resign to support Banerjee's entry via a bypoll, citing her past role in his political career and acknowledging her current challenges.

stories.title: 'SHAURYA: A father's promise' released by Harivansh, deputy chairman, Rajya Sabha, on International MPS Awareness Day 2026
stories.summary: On International MPS Awareness Day 2026, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh launched "SHAURYA: A Father's Promise" in Delhi. The book by Saurabh Singh chronicles his son's battle with MPS II, highlighting the struggles of rare disease families and advocating for a comprehensive National Rare Disease Policy.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: IRGC commander says Israel’s elimination 'achievable'; severe weather disrupts Delhi airport operations & more
stories.summary: An IRGC commander declared Israel's elimination achievable, backing Hezbollah amid regional tensions. Meanwhile, TMC rebels allege Abhishek Banerjee suppressed dissent post-election. China intensified Tiananmen Square crackdown commemorations, blocking victim families. Severe storms diverted flights in Delhi, while the BJP accused Kerala Congress of appeasement over an 'Islam-friendly gym' row.

stories.title: India edges past US to become 2nd globally in solar capacity additions in 2025
stories.summary: India has become the world's second-largest market for annual solar capacity additions, surpassing the US in 2025 with over 37 GW. The nation also ranks as the third-largest solar power producer globally. This rapid growth is attributed to strong policy support and infrastructure, accelerating India's clean energy transition.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu polls fallout: DMK to boycott INDIA bloc meet on June 8
Indian man Gurpinder Singh arrested for attempting to steal $495,000 from Florida woman
'Panic, uncertainty': Indian techie recalls moment when friends asked him to leave his own wedding and fly to US
UAE announces public holiday for Islamic New Year, three-day weekend for employees
Are fitness bands communication devices? Supreme Court to examine
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is examining whether fitness bands are communication devices, a classification disputed by importer GOQii Technologies. The company argues their devices are primarily measuring instruments, not for data transmission, but customs and a tribunal upheld the communication device classification due to Bluetooth connectivity and data sharing with coaches.

stories.title: 'You could not criticise Abhishek': TMC rebel explains the breaking point of dissent
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress rebels have voiced dissent against Abhishek Banerjee, citing a post-election meeting where criticism of his leadership was forbidden. Expelled MLA Sandipan Saha stated legislators were instructed to applaud Banerjee despite electoral setbacks, highlighting growing resentment over concentrated power.

stories.title: Forbidden anniversary: China blocks families from visiting graves of Tiananmen victims
stories.summary: China is intensifying its crackdown on any public remembrance of the 1989 Tiananmen Square events. Families of victims are being barred from visiting graves, and authorities are actively erasing the incident from public memory. This suppression escalates as Hong Kong also bans commemorations, while global reactions highlight ongoing censorship.

stories.title: 'Cong chooses Sharia': BJP reacts to 'Islam-friendly gym' in Kerala
Bachelors vs families: Who is the ‘ideal resident’? Inside India's housing society divide
stories.summary: A viral social media post ignited a debate on housing society rules, highlighting suspicions towards bachelors and young couples. While societies need regulations for smooth functioning, many residents feel unfairly scrutinized and stereotyped, leading to a clash between community order and personal autonomy.

stories.title: The magnetic wall that could replace drilling: A 29-year-old's breakthrough invention
Five Eyes issues 'unprecedented' warning over China's aggresive spying campaign
stories.summary: Chinese intelligence operatives are reportedly using fake job offers on professional platforms to ensnare government and military personnel. The Five Eyes alliance warns these tactics aim to extract sensitive information, with targets pressured to provide confidential details for financial rewards. Western nations urge vigilance against these sophisticated espionage efforts.

stories.title: Sri Lanka nursing home fire kills 12, owner arrested over negligence claims
A floating city: Inside $16 billion megaship that could house 80,000 people, complete with schools, restaurants and a 15,000-seat stadium
‘My childhood was taken away’: UK grooming gang survivor recalls abuse as 15 men jailed for 188 years
Missing nuclear scientist found dead after a year, skeletonized body with gunshot wound discovered in New Mexico forest
Vickrum Digwa, father and brother appear in court over weapons charges day after murder sentence
BJP counters Rahul Gandhi's 'economic tsunami' warning amid Iran war: 'Stop selling panic'
stories.summary: The BJP has strongly refuted Rahul Gandhi's "economic tsunami" warning, calling it fear-mongering. Party leader Amit Malviya highlighted India's economic resilience with strong indicators like rising E-way bills and FDI, asserting the government has implemented measures to protect citizens and businesses from global shocks, contrasting it with the UPA era's economic vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Honeybees just helped scientists build tiny drones that navigate without GPS and find their way home
Quote of the day by Amal Clooney: “We need young people with the courage to say...”
Labour MP Jess Asato sues Elon Musk's xAI over deepfake bikini images in landmark UK AI lawsuit
stories.summary: British Labour MP Jess Asato is suing Elon Musk's xAI, alleging its Grok chatbot generated fake sexualised images of her. The High Court case could set a precedent for AI developer accountability, focusing on system design rather than solely user actions. This legal challenge arrives as governments worldwide grapple with deepfake abuse and the need for stronger AI safeguards.

stories.title: Monsoon sets in over Kerala, marking beginning of rainy season in Ind
Hampshire police chief apologises over dying teen Henry Nowak’s arrest after Sikh man misled officers
Inside Onkalo: The world’s first nuclear waste vault built for 100,000 years of isolation
Vegan foods to get official FSSAI logo from July 2027
stories.summary: India's FSSAI has mandated a standardized green "Vegan" logo for all approved vegan food packages, effective July 1, 2027. This move aims to provide consumers with a clear, government-recognized mark, simplifying the identification of plant-based products and preventing misleading claims. The logo will help consumers confidently choose vegan options, distinguishing them from vegetarian products.

stories.title: Why no two people ever see the same rainbow: The science behind this beautifaul illusion
Mamata, Abhishek and 14 days of turmoil: How TMC's internal battle spilled into the open
stories.summary: On Wednesday, a group of 58 rebel MLAs led by expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee claimed control of the TMC legislature party after securing recognition from Assembly Speaker Rathindra Bose. The dramatic development capped nearly two weeks of mounting tensions fuelled by allegations of forged signatures, resentment over the growing influence of Abhishek Banerjee and an increasingly visible succession struggle within the organisation.

stories.title: 5300-year-old Europe’s oldest mummy may be ‘alive’: Scientists reveal shocking microbial activity
MIT scientists identify hidden brain cells that could boost memory far beyond current theories and explain why it has no known upper limit
Intelligence in an insect: Bumblebees break new ground with timing skills that baffle researchers
Was King Tut’s desert glass born from a cosmic explosion: New Zircon discovery sparks wild debate
'Not suicide': Rahul Gandhi blames 'broken system' after NEET aspirant's death; targets PM Modi
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi slammed the Modi government over the NEET-UG paper leak, citing the tragic suicide of aspirant Akanksha. He highlighted the farmer father's sacrifices and blamed the "corrupt, broken system" for her death. Gandhi also questioned Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's continued tenure and accused PM Modi of damaging India's education.

stories.title: Inside California’s 3-kilometre straight corridor: The 40-minute walk through the Klystron Gallery that never curves
8 years on, proposal for IAS-like medical cadre still awaiting states' views
stories.summary: A proposed All India Medical Service, envisioned to create a national cadre of doctors akin to IAS and IPS, remains under consideration by the Union health ministry. Despite years of consultations, the ministry is still awaiting responses from several states and Union Territories before proceeding with the plan.

stories.title: NIA raids ex-TMC MLA's house in Bengal pre-poll bomb blast probe
stories.summary: The investigation was transferred to the NIA following demands for a central inquiry into the explosion. Since assuming charge of the case, the agency has arrested several people, including TMC leader Wahidul Islam. Officials from a special NIA team arrived at Molla's residence to gather information and examine possible links to the case. During the operation, Molla's wife and daughter were seen entering the premises.

stories.title: 'I'm not running at all': Lalit Modi on the 'fugitive' tag and whether he'll return to India
stories.summary: Former IPL chairman Lalit Modi vehemently denies being a "fugitive," asserting he has never been convicted of any crime and labels the tag as media sensationalism. He argues that his global travel demonstrates he is not evading authorities, questioning the legal basis for any potential arrest after years of investigations.

stories.title: Trump says US, Iran to jointly remove buried nuclear material; Tehran sees no breakthrough in talks
US charges tech CEO over alleged exports of restricted equipment to Iran
'Lack of effort' to free Imran Khan? Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf lawmakers revolt against party leadership
stories.summary: A significant internal rift has emerged within PTI in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as lawmakers express dissatisfaction with the party leadership's efforts to secure Imran Khan's release. Disgruntled MPAs, reportedly denied cabinet positions, have penned a letter to the PTI chairman, arguing the release campaign has lost momentum and become ineffective.

stories.title: "I was so scared": Pokimane's nightmare birthday trip began with a medical emergency doctors rarely see
stories.summary: Twitch star Pokimane revealed she nearly suffered a serious eye injury before her 30th birthday trip to Paris. After experiencing severe pain and irritation, an emergency optometrist discovered an eyelash lodged inside a tear duct, a condition the doctor reportedly had never seen before. The eyelash was removed successfully, allowing Pokimane to travel. Her France trip later faced additional challenges, including accommodation issues and refund disputes.

stories.title: DKS is Karnataka captain, but Siddaramaiah’s XI dominate team
stories.summary: D.K. Shivakumar sworn in as Karnataka's 24th CM, with G. Parameshwara as Deputy CM. The new cabinet balances caste and regional interests, reflecting Siddaramaiah's influence. Early initiatives focus on youth welfare, including free student bus passes and a private job portal. The ceremony highlighted religious traditions and drew national Congress leaders.

stories.title: New details surface as ChudTheBuilder’s release bid stalls despite Alex Rosen offering $100,000 toward bond
stories.summary: Dalton Eatherly, known as ChudTheBuilder, remains jailed after a Tennessee judge refused to lower his $1 million bond. YouTuber Alex Rosen offered $100,000 toward the bond, but Judge William Goodman III kept existing restrictions. Eatherly also faces separate charges in Nashville. The main case stems from a May 13 courthouse shooting involving Joshua Fox in Clarksville.

stories.title: Cabinet backs ordinance to ease tax rules for foreign investors in some securities
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has recommended an ordinance to ease tax rules for foreign investors in certain securities, aiming to strengthen the rupee. This move follows significant foreign portfolio investor withdrawals and addresses concerns raised by FPIs regarding capital gains and securities transaction taxes.

stories.title: Flex-fuel vehicles practical solution to reduce crude imports: Hardeep Singh Puri
“Bro in a wheelchair?”: Clavicular’s new rhinoplasty recovery photos spark leg lengthening surgery speculation
stories.summary: Clavicular’s post-surgery photos have become a major talking point online. While the images clearly show him recovering from rhinoplasty, the leg braces and wheelchair seen in one photo led to widespread speculation about possible additional procedures. So far, no confirmed information has been released about any surgery other than the rhinoplasty, leaving many questions unanswered.

stories.title: Public sector bank accounts not needed for re-evaluation fee: CBSE
stories.summary: CBSE has clarified that students applying for Class XII answer sheet verification and re-evaluation can use various online payment options, not just specific bank accounts. The board also confirmed its online portal is functioning smoothly despite a significant cyberattack attempt shortly after its launch. Over 43,000 applications have been processed so far.

stories.title: UK foreign secretary arrives in India for talks with PM Modi, EAM Jaishankar
stories.summary: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is in India for her inaugural official visit, aiming to mitigate economic impacts of current conflicts and bolster global stability. She will meet with counterpart S Jaishankar and Prime Minister Modi to advance engagement, building on recent efforts to expedite the UK-India Free Trade Agreement.

stories.title: SC collegium recommends 10 new judges for three HCs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court collegium, led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, has recommended ten advocates and judicial officers for appointment as judges to the High Courts of Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh. The recommendations include six advocates for the Karnataka HC, three judicial officers for the Himachal Pradesh HC, and one advocate for the Madhya Pradesh HC.

stories.title: CJP: Have no political links, fight bigger than any party
stories.summary: Ahead of a June 6 protest, the satirical platform Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) appointed three spokespersons to address public anger over examination controversies. The group, demanding the Education Minister's resignation, dismissed claims of being proxies for political opponents, emphasizing their fight is larger than individual affiliations.

stories.title: Congress to cadre: Ignore CJP, focus on NEET-CBSE stir
stories.summary: Congress plans to intensify its agitation on NEET-CBSE controversies over the next fortnight, urging members to focus on student and youth issues. The party is wary of rival political parties using the protests for their own agenda, drawing parallels to past movements. Youth Congress and NSUI are holding nationwide protests, emphasizing NEET as their primary concern.

stories.title: After PM Modi’s nudge, mantris carpool to reach cabinet meet at Seva Teerth
stories.summary: Several Union ministers carpooled to a cabinet meeting at Seva Teerth. This follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call to reduce vehicle fleets. Ministers like Nitin Gadkari, J P Nadda, Ashwini Vaishnaw, and Mansukh Mandaviya shared rides. This initiative emphasizes sustainability and leads by example amid global energy concerns. Earlier, ministers and chief ministers had reduced their convoys.

stories.title: PM Modi: Nepal is India's priority partner
On June 10, Modi will break Nehru’s record of longest elected PM stint
stories.summary: Narendra Modi is set to become the longest-serving unbroken head of government in India, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru on June 10. Modi's tenure, beginning May 26, 2014, will reach 4,399 days, just ahead of Nehru's 4,398 days. This milestone highlights a significant shift in Indian political leadership and policy direction.

stories.title: Who is Hasan Piker’s mom Ülker Sedef? Report links her to streamer’s college transfer after low GPA
stories.summary: Hasan Piker’s mother, Ülker Sedef Piker, is an art and architectural historian with degrees from Rutgers University and the New Jersey Institute of Technology. A recent New York Post report claimed Hasan transferred from the University of Miami to Rutgers after earning a 2.9 GPA. Hasan has often praised his mother, calling her a major source of inspiration.

stories.title: If TMC splits, speaker's role key in recognising 'real party'
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress faces a significant crisis with a faction claiming majority MLA support. The West Bengal assembly speaker's role is crucial in identifying the "original party," a decision guided by the Supreme Court's directives on party constitution and leadership structure outside the assembly, not just legislative numbers.

stories.title: SC: Cops abusing authority must be dealt with sternly
stories.summary: The Supreme Court sternly stated that police officers abusing their position must face strict consequences, as normal presumptions for accused individuals won't apply. It cancelled anticipatory bail for three Maharashtra police officers accused of harassing a family and extorting money after a search on a train.

stories.title: Can bar overqualified person from job: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that individuals with qualifications exceeding the maximum prescribed for a job can be disqualified. This decision aims to ensure employment opportunities for those with lower educational attainment, preventing overqualified candidates from displacing genuinely eligible applicants.

stories.title: Winds of change in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu may steady NDA's ship in Parliament
stories.summary: The BJP-led NDA sees a smoother legislative path as key opposition rivals TMC and DMK face internal challenges. A split within TMC and DMK's strained ties with Congress create opportunities for the ruling coalition to advance its agenda, including simultaneous elections, with renewed vigor.

Indian national charged in crash that killed teen, victim’s mother calls for deportation
Indian national charged in crash that killed teen, victim’s mother calls for deportation
Princess Diana's forgotten letter reveals what she wanted for Prince William and Prince Harry's future
Speculation mounts over TMC’s MPs, its heft in INDIA bloc
stories.summary: The Trinamool Congress faces a significant internal crisis in West Bengal, raising questions about its national parliamentary strength and its role within the INDIA bloc. With a crucial opposition meeting scheduled, Mamata Banerjee's party is strategizing to maintain unity among its MPs and counter the BJP's influence amidst these developments.

stories.title: Day after texting brother about new job, Kolkata girl run over in UK by driver charged with DUI
stories.summary: A 28-year-old Kolkata woman, Anisha Chakraborty, was tragically killed in a hit-and-run incident in Birmingham, UK, just after completing her master's degree. She was on her way home from a pub outing when a black Audi RSQ8 struck her. Her family is awaiting the repatriation of her body, while a GoFundMe campaign has been launched to support the costs.

stories.title: On Indo-China border, model village to come up in Ladakh for nomads
stories.summary: Ladakh's first model border village is being established at Chumur, a remote settlement at 16,700 feet along the India-China border. This initiative under the Vibrant Village Program will provide climate-resilient housing, enhance livelihoods through goat rearing and greenhouse cultivation, and integrate essential services to foster secure, permanent settlements and strengthen civil-defence cooperation.

stories.title: UK YouTuber murdered pregnant girlfriend and tried to hide it through a gaming livestream
National Conference’s ‘secretive’ Dachigam huddle ends with Delhi protest plan for J&K statehood
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah convened a strategy session with National Conference MLAs and MPs at Dachigam National Park. The meeting concluded with a call for a protest in New Delhi during Parliament's monsoon session, demanding the restoration of J&K's statehood. The party also resolved to push for a ban on liquor in the region.

stories.title: IRCTC flags 9 crore user accounts, expands AI monitoring across railway kitchens
stories.summary: IRCTC has taken decisive action against ticket booking fraud, deactivating over three crore suspicious user IDs and verifying six crore more. Simultaneously, an AI-powered kitchen monitoring system, utilizing 2,394 cameras, now oversees 800 kitchens, detecting nine types of hygiene issues to ensure food quality for millions of passengers.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Leonardo da Vinci: “A painter should begin every canvas with a wash of black, because all things in nature are…”
US visa holder denied entry at Los Angeles airport after previous visit, held in CBP custody
Kick streamer Clavicular chased a new look through live rhinoplasty and left viewers speechless
stories.summary: Looksmaxxing streamer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, livestreamed his rhinoplasty on Kick on June 3 with celebrity plastic surgeon Dr. Michael Salzhauer, also known as Dr. Miami. The surgery lasted about two hours and drew nearly 6,000 average viewers. The broadcast quickly went viral, with some viewers intrigued and others uncomfortable watching cosmetic surgery live.

stories.title: 'Entering H1-B lottery...': Indian students may face tougher path to US jobs under new visa rule
Chicago student kicked out of graduation ceremony, denied diploma after doing 'split' on stage
'It's not nice': Donald Trump says US has 'other way' to deal with Iran
Three British Navy personnel killed in helicopter crash during training exercise in Devon, MOD confirms
'We would not fly in this visibility': Indian-origin pilot's warning before helicopter crash
'Any Indian who supported Vickrum Digwa must be...': UK MP issues warning after Henry Nowak murder
‘I was a little bit perturbed’: Trump confirms calling Netanyahu 'crazy'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump admitted calling Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu "f***ing crazy" due to frustration over Lebanon escalation, impacting Iran talks. Despite the heated exchange, Trump insists their strong working relationship continues, citing shared "wartime leader" pressures. He remains optimistic about resolving regional tensions soon.

stories.title: The dark side of plastic recycling: Why some waste ends up being burned
